title: Republican John James seeks some distance from Trump in Michigan governor debate
summary: Democrat Jocelyn Benson repeatedly tried to tie James, a Trump-backed congressman, to the president during their first showdown ahead of the November election.
story: Republican Rep. John James on Tuesday sought to put some daylight between himself and President Donald Trump as he debated his opponent in the Michigan governor’s race.

Democratic nominee Jocelyn Benson, Michigan’s secretary of state, repeatedly tried to tie James to Trump during the hourlong showdown, saying he had failed to stand up to Trump and wouldn’t do so as governor, either.
James, who was boosted by Trump’s endorsement in his GOP primary campaign, pointed to the Iran war and tariff policy as issues over which he has disagreements with Trump.
“I’ve stood up to the president many times. I’ve said that I can agree with the president without worshipping him. I can disagree without attacking him, and I always put Michigan first,” James said.

James said he believed the conflict in Iran needed to end “quickly, as in yesterday,” echoing comments he made last month. James, who has voted against several resolutions in the House that sought to end the Iran war, also said he wants to “use whatever checks and balance power that we have to bring this war to a swift conclusion.”

His comments in his first debate with Benson in the key battleground state come as polls show voters nationally continuing to sour on Trump’s handling of the Iran war and the cost of living as the midterm elections draw closer.
Benson attacked James for voting against the Iran war powers resolutions while blaming high gas prices on the conflict.

“I struggle with that vote,” James said of the war powers resolutions votes. “I’m a combat veteran. I have been to war. She has not. I understand what war means, and so I voted to protect the troops and to fund them while they were in harm’s way.”
Benson pointed out that her husband served in the Army.
“Military spouses serve also, congressman,” she said.
Benson sought to link James to Trump’s tariff agenda, saying she dubs them the “John James tax,” while James said he had pushed back on the Trump administration’s tariffs against Canada.

“I’ve actually called out the administration specifically, talking with the trade ambassador and saying that we must get back to the table, stop acting like children and negotiate a reciprocal, fair and mutually beneficial arrangement to make sure that we can bring our jobs back and protect our industry,” James said.
For Subscribers

James, who promised in July to “back law enforcement, end sanctuary city policies” and “cooperate with federal immigration authorities to remove criminal illegal immigrants,” seemed to soften that stance Tuesday, saying he does not see a need for ICE presence in Michigan.
For Subscribers

“We’re going to be cooperating with federal law enforcement as well as our communities. We’re going to make sure that we’re prioritizing violent offenders, and we’re going to make sure that we enforce the law,” he said. “Frankly, I don’t believe we’re going to need ICE presence in the state of Michigan, because we are going to be enforcing the law.”
James tried to tie Benson’s record to that of term-limited Democratic Gov. Gretchen Whitmer.

Asked by moderator Rick Albin of NBC affiliate WOOD of Grand Rapids to point to a decision about which Whitmer did not listen to Michiganders, Benson did not cite a specific policy but said, “Where I think we need to listen to the people ... is a way to improve our Department of Health and Human Services.”

The candidates also clashed over data centers amid a growing public backlash to them, each accusing the other of profiting from them. Benson accused James of having voted for policies friendly to data centers while holding stocks in them, and James accused Benson’s family of profiting from one center’s construction. Benson denied that her family had profited from them, while James said any data center-related stocks he owns were held in broad mutual funds.

The nationally watched Michigan Senate race, in which the Democratic candidate, Abdul El-Sayed, is running against GOP former Rep. Mike Rogers, did not come up Tuesday. Republicans in particular have been eager to tie El-Sayed, a progressive, to other Democratic candidates in competitive races.
Neither candidate mentioned that race or tried to tie the other to either Senate nominee.

Democrats are looking to keep Michigan’s governorship in their party’s hands after Whitmer’s two terms in office. Trump carried the state by just over 1 percentage point in the 2024 presidential election. NBC News characterizes the race as leaning toward Democrats.
Benson and James are scheduled to debate again on Oct. 15.

title: Georgia governor candidates spar over the economy and Trump in lone debate
summary: Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms and Republican Rick Jackson clashed Tuesday night during their only scheduled debate of this fall’s race for governor in Georgia.
story: Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms and Republican Rick Jackson clashed Tuesday night during their only scheduled debate of this fall’s race for governor in Georgia, taking aim at each other on economic issues, data centers and President Donald Trump.

Public polls show Bottoms, the former mayor of Atlanta and a former Biden administration official, and Jackson, a billionaire healthcare executive, locked in a close race four weeks out from Election Day, with early voting kicking off next week.

The hourlong, town-hall-style debate was largely civil, featuring live and taped questions from voters. Jackson frequently ripped his opponent over her record as mayor, while Bottoms attacked his praise of Trump.

“My opponent has said he wants to be Trump’s favorite governor. He wants to be Trump with a Southern tone. He said there’s not a single policy that he disagrees with Trump on,” Bottoms said in response to a question about the Trump administration’s cuts to federal funding.
“I will stand up to Donald Trump when necessary. I’m not running to be his favorite governor,” she continued.
Jackson responded, “I don’t owe anybody anything,” and said, “Nobody’s ever told me what to do.”
He then invoked Brian Kemp, Georgia’s popular, term-limited governor — the first of multiple times he did so.
“I will stand up to anybody, just like Brian Kemp has done. He works with both parties, both presidents, and he stands up when he disagrees,” Jackson said.

Trump endorsed Jackson’s rival, Lt. Gov. Burt Jones, during the Republican gubernatorial primary. But Jackson still attempted to claim the MAGA mantle and leaned heavily into comparing himself to the president. Since winning the nomination in June, he’s backed off that approach and sought to link himself more to Kemp, who had also backed Jones.

Jackson took several shots at Bottoms over her tenure as mayor, accusing her of being responsible for regional inflation in the Atlanta area that he claimed exceeded national inflation rates and pointing to higher crime rates in the city during the Covid-19 pandemic.
“This is the kind of policy that we cannot have in running Georgia, not having people feeling safe to go to work,” Jackson said. “Bad mayors don’t make good governors.”

While the candidates were asked about housing and education, the event focused predominantly on economic issues and affordability, with both candidates repeatedly pressed about how they’d bring down costs. Both focused heavily on tax relief.

Bottoms emphasized her proposals to cut or suspend state or local taxes on a raft of items, like auto insurance, groceries, hygiene products and diapers. Jackson reiterated his promise to cut state income taxes, property taxes and taxes on certain utilities.
For Subscribers
Data centers and the controversial surveillance traffic cameras known as Flock cameras also took center stage.
For Subscribers

On data centers, Bottoms repeated her desire to implement a pause on new construction. Jackson said he wouldn’t approve new construction as governor without first getting local community approval, establishing environmental standards and getting a commitment that local communities’ power bills would be reduced.
But the two sparred over the issue, as well, with Bottoms accusing Jackson of investing in data centers and Jackson accusing her of having approved building them as mayor.
Bottoms also said she wasn’t opposed to a moratorium on installing new Flock cameras, while Jackson said he was.
The issue of election security — which has hung over Georgia politics for six years — also came up.
Bottoms said she was “deeply concerned about Donald Trump’s rhetoric around our elections.”
Jackson, however, when he was asked whether he thought the U.S. Justice Department should be “overseeing and getting involved” in the state’s elections, deferred to Kemp again.
“I don’t think that’s necessary unless Gov. Kemp thinks it’s necessary,” he said.
Jackson has flooded the airwaves with ads, using tens of millions of dollars of his own money to outspend Bottoms 7-to-1 as of last week.
That disparity has worried many Democrats, who’ve seen this year as a prime opportunity to flip the governorship blue for the first time in 16 years.
Aiding Bottoms is the broader political environment in Georgia and nationally: Trump faces negative approval ratings and voter concerns about his administration’s handling of the economy.

title: Zach Lahn’s residency history and Rob Sand’s party come under fire in first Iowa governor debate
summary: Lahn, the Republican nominee, and Sand, the Democratic state auditor, are running to succeed retiring GOP Gov. Kim Reynolds.
story: Republican Zach Lahn and Democrat Rob Sand repeatedly returned to one topic in their first debate Tuesday night in the race to be Iowa’s next governor: questions about Lahn’s residency history in the state.

Sand, the state auditor, and Lahn, a businessman, met in Davenport as they run to succeed retiring Republican Gov. Kim Reynolds in an unusually competitive race for a state that has trended to the right in recent years.

Iowa has not had a Democrat in the governor’s mansion since Chet Culver was defeated in 2010, and Sand is the only Democrat currently elected statewide. While Sand has cast himself as an independent-minded candidate, Lahn labeled him a “radical liberal” and a “career politician” who supports liberal positions on taxes and immigration.

As the two men sparred over tax rates, economic growth, addressing the state’s cancer crisis and other issues on NBC affiliate KWQC, both repeatedly referred to the controversy over Lahn’s reported ties to Kansas, which include public records showing he voted there in 2018, 2020 and 2022 before he registered in Iowa in 2024.
Lahn responded Tuesday to reports that he still frequently flies to a second home in Kansas.
“I’m a sixth-generation Iowan. I live in Iowa today. I have lived in Iowa. Rob has been lying about this, and the issue is I have a blended family, and my kids split time,” he said.

The subject first arose in a conversation about education. Sand advocated for increasing teacher salaries and better oversight of the use of public funding, while Lahn called for stronger auditing of the school voucher system and limiting the program to lower-income families.
“I want to be the biggest advocate for public school kids in the state,” Lahn said.

Sand responded: “I don’t think you’re going to be the biggest advocate for public school students over a guy who sends his kids there. When you were running advertisements saying that Marxists have hijacked the curriculum in Iowa, Zach, I’m pretty sure that that’s just more evidence that you don’t spend enough time in Iowa.”
Lahn called the attacks “the central lie of Rob Sand’s campaign.”
The controversy has been a drag on Lahn’s campaign, with Sand holding an advantage in public polling ahead of November’s election.
Throughout the debate, Lahn lambasted Sand as a “liberal billionaire” backed by his wife’s family’s money.

Sand’s wife, Christine, is the CEO of her family’s company, the Lauridsen Group, which owns several food and health product companies. Her family has donated more than $12 million to Sand’s campaigns over the years, having backed him since he first ran for state auditor.
Earlier in the night, the candidates were asked how they would address Iowa’s low economic growth rate and the question of affordability on Day 1 in office.
Lahn said he would prioritize homegrown businesses and make sure state government was “not prioritizing big out-of-state projects that are not employing people, like data centers.”

He did indicate he would support tax incentives for the White House-backed $15 billion steel mill project announced last week. He also praised President Donald Trump’s executive action loosening restrictions on tax-exempt “red dye diesel” fuel used for farm vehicles, which he said he proposed to Vice President JD Vance when he visited Iowa last month.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

The rising cost of diesel, now $6.05 per gallon in Iowa, has been a major concern for farmers in the state, who have also felt the squeeze from rising fertilizer prices and tariffs, threatening the campaigns of GOP candidates in the heartland.

Sand called for a cap on utility fees, ending the privatization of Medicaid in Iowa, raising the minimum wage — which he has said should be set at $12 an hour — and importing prescription drugs from Canada.
Lahn wouldn’t commit to raise the minimum wage, which was last raised in Iowa in 2009 and is at $7.25 an hour. He said he would focus on industry deconsolidation and lowering taxes.

“We’ve had some great efforts to lower taxes for the people of Iowa, and Rob, you’ve opposed those efforts at every step,” Lahn shot at his opponent. “And so I think we have to be very honest here about where we’re standing. Rob is supporting the raising of taxes because that’s what liberals do: They want to raise taxes. I’m here to cut taxes.”
Asked to respond, Sand denied that he wants to raise taxes.

Both candidates made a point to address cancer rates in their opening statements. Iowa is one of three states where the incidence of cancer is increasing amid environmental risks associated with chemicals used by the agriculture industry, like glyphosate, PFAS and nitrates.
“Iowa is at a point where we are at the bottom for economic growth; we’re at the top for cancer growth,” Sand said.
Lahn cited “the fastest rate of new cancer in the country” as one of three issues that motivated him to run for office.

Lahn, who is backed by prominent members of the “Make America Healthy Again” movement, has made cancer rates a centerpiece of his campaign, frequently targeting the powerful agriculture industry. He called addressing cancer a “foundational question” and the “crisis of our generation.”
“For a very long time, we have seen the nitrate load in our water increase year after year,” he said. “We have to start to put in place real solutions.”
He voiced support for the state’s IWiLL program (Iowa’s Water and Land Legacy) to address water quality issues and high nitrate levels.

“I’m glad that Mr. Lahn brought up IWiLL and mentioned that he’s been supporting it and talking about it since he started the campaign. I’m glad that he’s been doing that,” Sand said. “I actually voted for it in 2010 because I lived here. You didn’t.”

title: Global bond sell-off pushes U.S. Treasury yields to fresh 24-year highs
summary: The yield on key U.S. Treasury bonds rose to fresh 24-year highs Wednesday, as the latest global bond sell-off picked up steam.
story: The yield on key U.S. Treasury bonds rose to fresh 24-year highs Wednesday, as the latest global bond sell-off picked up steam.

Benchmark government bonds in France and Italy also rose sharply and were on pace for their biggest one-day jump since March, when the launch of the Iran war rattled global markets. The yield on the U.K. 30-year government bond hit its highest level since 1998.
When bonds fall, their yields rise.
Closely tracking those moves, the 10-year Treasury yield rose as high as 5.35% and the 30-year Treasury yield hit 5.73% — the highest levels for each since 2002.
The bond rout sent stocks tumbling, as investors bet that rising bond yields would raise corporate borrowing costs and cut into profits.
Europe’s broad Stoxx 600 index fell 1%. Benchmark indexes in France and Germany were off by more than 1%, and stocks in Italy on the country’s FTSE MIB index slid nearly 2.5%.
U.S. stocks also dipped Wednesday morning, just a day after both the Nasdaq and S&P 500 closed at record highs. In early trading, the S&P 500 was down 0.6% and the Nasdaq Composite declined by 0.8%.
For Subscribers
As stocks fell, oil prices ticked up, adding pressure to bond yields. Brent crude oil rose 1% in early trading, to more than $102 per barrel.
The Treasury Department will sell a $39 billion tranche of flagship 10-year notes at 2 p.m. ET Wednesday, and investors will be closely watching how markets react.
The recent rise in bond yields only adds more pain to governments that have seen their borrowing costs soar since the start of the year.
Overnight, International Monetary Fund chief Kristalina Georgieva warned that governments urgently need to take steps to get their unprecedented debt under control.
For Subscribers
She also predicted that government bond yields around the world would remain under pressure because of the ever-expanding artificial intelligence boom.

“Policymakers had a relatively easy ride over the last 17 years, as for all that time interest rates were stuck below GDP growth rates,” Georgieva said in a Bloomberg Television interview. “Higher interest rates now put an end to that.”

Her comments followed multiple reports that Elon Musk’s SpaceX is planning to raise $40 billion in cash to buy AI chips from Nvidia. NBC News has not independently confirmed the reports and SpaceX did not immediately reply to a request for comment.

But if the company follows through, that borrowed $40 billion would join hundreds of billions more in bond sales by AI-linked companies in recent years. The companies are using the money to build data centers and buy equipment with which to fill them.
Some economists believe that the vast sums of money being borrowed by private AI companies could pile additional pressure on government bond yields.
“France may be on the verge of a full-blown debt crisis,” wrote Ed Yardeni, president of Yardeni Research on Sunday.

He noted that the yield on French 10-year government bonds has risen the most of any major economy this year. Coming in second  is the United States, while Italy, a country traditionally viewed as far more risky by the bond markets, comes in third.

Apollo economic strategist Huw van Steenis wrote in a Wednesday note, “Hyperscalers have raised $48 billion in bonds in European currencies this year, which is already more than triple the entire amount of 2025.”

title: They were a historically bad team. Now they’re a threat to make the World Series.
summary: The Chicago White Sox are up 2-0 in the American League Division Series, a shocking turnaround after three straight 100-loss seasons.
story: CHICAGO — Many Chicago White Sox fans were genuinely cheering for the team to lose just two years ago.

In late September 2024, the White Sox were taking the field for their final home series of the season. The attendance was sparse, but those who did show up were hoping to witness history, as Chicago was one defeat away from setting the record for losses in a 162-game season. The White Sox, of course, let them down, winning their final three home games before they lost their record 121st game on the road in their next series.
Fast-forward to today, and the unthinkable has happened: The White Sox are returning home as heroes.

Chicago will play its first playoff game at home since 2021 on Wednesday. And the White Sox will enter their matchup with the Cleveland Guardians up 2-0 in the American League Division Series, one win away from advancing to the Championship Series.
The five years between home playoff games were not kind to fans of the South Siders.

After a respectable 81-81 finish in 2022, Chicago nosedived. The White Sox lost 101 games in 2023, 121 in 2024 and 102 more last year. This season, they became the first team to make the playoffs after back-to-back 100-loss seasons — which also means they’re the first team to do so after three straight 100-loss seasons.
On Wednesday, the Sox will have another chance at history, as they haven’t clinched a playoff series in front of their home fans since 1906.

The fans have been “waiting 120 years, so maybe we can do it this year,” pitcher Grant Taylor, who recorded saves in each of the first two wins against the Guardians, told reporters Monday. “I think it’s going to be unbelievable. Those fans deserve it. They’ve been with us for three years of 100 losses, and they’ve been with us a good bit this year giving us a lot of support as we’ve gone through this. So being able to give them a postseason game is going to be pretty special.”
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

Chicago has turned over most of its team since the 2024 season. Only four hitters and five players were on the roster then and now, per MLB.com. The White Sox have improved through several avenues since.

In the offseason, they signed Japanese slugger Munetaka Murakami. Murakami, 26, blasted 35 homers in his first MLB regular season, and he has added one more through his first four playoff appearances. (Murakami also captured the attention of fans thanks to his enthusiastic postgame interviews.)

Meanwhile, pitchers such as Taylor and starter Sean Burke have emerged after having been drafted years ago. Taylor had a 2.25 ERA in 84 innings during the regular season. Burke struck out 185 batters across 32 appearances (including 27 starts) and finished 17th among all pitchers in wins above replacement.

In addition to an explosive offense that was top 10 in both home runs and slugging percentage during the regular season, the White Sox have employed a unique pitching strategy, relying heavily on their relievers to throw multiple innings.

“We knew we had to be different,” general manager Chris Getz told MLB Network this month. “It became leaning into those arms. What’s the pathway to win? How do we solve today? Oftentimes it was getting creative with openers. Thankfully, we’ve got some arms that can go multiple innings.”

(It’s also possible the team’s success is coming from a higher power, as Pope Leo XIV is a fan. “I willingly invoke the Almighty’s abundant blessings upon you and your loved ones,” the pope wrote in a letter to the team in September.)
The man in charge of the dugout is Will Venable, who played in the majors from 2008 to 2016. Venable became Chicago’s manager in October 2024 and has become a key part of the franchise’s turnaround.

“For where the organization was and the pain of those couple years in which there was 100-loss seasons, to see the growth and have the fans be a part of this and be able to celebrate this, it makes me happy for everyone involved with White Sox baseball,” Venable said after the White Sox won in the wild-card round.

As impressive as the revival has been so far, the Sox don’t seem simply happy to be here. Asked in September what Chicago could do in the playoffs, designated hitter Andrew Benintendi told MLB.com his team was “confident.”
Added Benintendi: “We are dumb enough to think we can win it. So, why not?”

title: Cornell students plan seven-hour sit-in over alleged 2024 fraternity assault
summary: Cornell University students are expected to hold a seven-hour sit-in Wednesday in solidarity with Jane Doe, the woman who alleges she was sexually assaulted by members of the Chi Phi fraternity nearly two years ago.
story: Cornell University students are expected to hold a seven-hour sit-in Wednesday in solidarity with Jane Doe, the woman who alleges she was sexually assaulted by members of the Chi Phi fraternity nearly two years ago.
“Seven hours for the seven hours she endured. Seven hours of solidarity. Seven hours demanding change,” a coalition of Cornell student groups said in a post on Instagram announcing the demonstration.

The students are expected to gather inside a campus dining hall named for Pulitzer Prize-winning author Toni Morrison starting at 1:30 p.m. ET, according to the announcement. The organizers said the planned sit-in is part of “Zero Day,” an “economic blackout calling on students to disrupt business as usual by not attending class or spending on campus.”

The protest illustrates the tense mood on the Ivy League campus following Jane Doe’s allegations that she was sexually assaulted and plied with drugs Oct. 19-20, 2024. She filed a civil lawsuit against the university and seven fraternity members last month, leading to renewed national attention on sexual misconduct and collegiate Greek life.
Three of the accused men have publicly denied the allegations through attorneys.

The sit-in comes two days after Cornell faculty members introduced a resolution calling for a no-confidence vote in the university administration over its handling of the alleged assault at the Chi Phi fraternity house. The resolution was submitted to the University Faculty Committee on Monday night, according to a copy obtained by NBC News.
For Subscribers

Cornell has drawn intense scrutiny over how it responded to Jane Doe’s allegations in November 2024, and Tompkins County District Attorney Matthew Van Houten has been criticized for declining to charge the accused. The university and the district attorney have each defended their original 2024 probes.
For Subscribers

New York Gov. Kathy Hochul effectively replaced Van Houten as lead investigator last week, appointing state Attorney General Letitia James to oversee the case. Cornell and Van Houten have publicly welcomed James’ involvement. “I trust that she will examine the facts and apply the law,” Van Houten said in a statement on Friday.

Wednesday’s sit-in was announced on Instagram by a group of campus organizations, including Black Students United, Cornell NAACP, Mecha de Cornell, Planned Parenthood Generation Action at Cornell, Students for a Democratic Cornell, and a student-run chapter of the American Civil Liberties Union.
“The sit-in will be a space for students to share their support for survivors of sexual violence in myriad ways, including the share of resources and teach-ins,” the student groups said on Instagram.

title: Global bond sell-off pushes U.S. Treasury yields to fresh 24-year highs
summary: The yield on key U.S. Treasury bonds rose to fresh 24-year highs Wednesday, as the latest global bond sell-off picked up steam.
story: The yield on key U.S. Treasury bonds rose to fresh 24-year highs Wednesday, as the latest global bond sell-off picked up steam.

Benchmark government bonds in France and Italy also rose sharply and were on pace for their biggest one-day jump since March, when the launch of the Iran war rattled global markets. The yield on the U.K. 30-year government bond hit its highest level since 1998.
When bonds fall, their yields rise.
Closely tracking those moves, the 10-year Treasury yield rose as high as 5.35% and the 30-year Treasury yield hit 5.73% — the highest levels for each since 2002.
The bond rout sent stocks tumbling, as investors bet that rising bond yields would raise corporate borrowing costs and cut into profits.
Europe’s broad Stoxx 600 index fell 1%. Benchmark indexes in France and Germany were off by more than 1%, and stocks in Italy on the country’s FTSE MIB index slid nearly 2.5%.
U.S. stocks also dipped Wednesday morning, just a day after both the Nasdaq and S&P 500 closed at record highs. In early trading, the S&P 500 was down 0.6% and the Nasdaq Composite declined by 0.8%.
For Subscribers
As stocks fell, oil prices ticked up, adding pressure to bond yields. Brent crude oil rose 1% in early trading, to more than $102 per barrel.
The Treasury Department will sell a $39 billion tranche of flagship 10-year notes at 2 p.m. ET Wednesday, and investors will be closely watching how markets react.
The recent rise in bond yields only adds more pain to governments that have seen their borrowing costs soar since the start of the year.
Overnight, International Monetary Fund chief Kristalina Georgieva warned that governments urgently need to take steps to get their unprecedented debt under control.
For Subscribers
She also predicted that government bond yields around the world would remain under pressure because of the ever-expanding artificial intelligence boom.

“Policymakers had a relatively easy ride over the last 17 years, as for all that time interest rates were stuck below GDP growth rates,” Georgieva said in a Bloomberg Television interview. “Higher interest rates now put an end to that.”

Her comments followed multiple reports that Elon Musk’s SpaceX is planning to raise $40 billion in cash to buy AI chips from Nvidia. NBC News has not independently confirmed the reports and SpaceX did not immediately reply to a request for comment.

But if the company follows through, that borrowed $40 billion would join hundreds of billions more in bond sales by AI-linked companies in recent years. The companies are using the money to build data centers and buy equipment with which to fill them.
Some economists believe that the vast sums of money being borrowed by private AI companies could pile additional pressure on government bond yields.
“France may be on the verge of a full-blown debt crisis,” wrote Ed Yardeni, president of Yardeni Research on Sunday.

He noted that the yield on French 10-year government bonds has risen the most of any major economy this year. Coming in second  is the United States, while Italy, a country traditionally viewed as far more risky by the bond markets, comes in third.

Apollo economic strategist Huw van Steenis wrote in a Wednesday note, “Hyperscalers have raised $48 billion in bonds in European currencies this year, which is already more than triple the entire amount of 2025.”

title: They were a historically bad team. Now they’re a threat to make the World Series.
summary: The Chicago White Sox are up 2-0 in the American League Division Series, a shocking turnaround after three straight 100-loss seasons.
story: CHICAGO — Many Chicago White Sox fans were genuinely cheering for the team to lose just two years ago.

In late September 2024, the White Sox were taking the field for their final home series of the season. The attendance was sparse, but those who did show up were hoping to witness history, as Chicago was one defeat away from setting the record for losses in a 162-game season. The White Sox, of course, let them down, winning their final three home games before they lost their record 121st game on the road in their next series.
Fast-forward to today, and the unthinkable has happened: The White Sox are returning home as heroes.

Chicago will play its first playoff game at home since 2021 on Wednesday. And the White Sox will enter their matchup with the Cleveland Guardians up 2-0 in the American League Division Series, one win away from advancing to the Championship Series.
The five years between home playoff games were not kind to fans of the South Siders.

After a respectable 81-81 finish in 2022, Chicago nosedived. The White Sox lost 101 games in 2023, 121 in 2024 and 102 more last year. This season, they became the first team to make the playoffs after back-to-back 100-loss seasons — which also means they’re the first team to do so after three straight 100-loss seasons.
On Wednesday, the Sox will have another chance at history, as they haven’t clinched a playoff series in front of their home fans since 1906.

The fans have been “waiting 120 years, so maybe we can do it this year,” pitcher Grant Taylor, who recorded saves in each of the first two wins against the Guardians, told reporters Monday. “I think it’s going to be unbelievable. Those fans deserve it. They’ve been with us for three years of 100 losses, and they’ve been with us a good bit this year giving us a lot of support as we’ve gone through this. So being able to give them a postseason game is going to be pretty special.”
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

Chicago has turned over most of its team since the 2024 season. Only four hitters and five players were on the roster then and now, per MLB.com. The White Sox have improved through several avenues since.

In the offseason, they signed Japanese slugger Munetaka Murakami. Murakami, 26, blasted 35 homers in his first MLB regular season, and he has added one more through his first four playoff appearances. (Murakami also captured the attention of fans thanks to his enthusiastic postgame interviews.)

Meanwhile, pitchers such as Taylor and starter Sean Burke have emerged after having been drafted years ago. Taylor had a 2.25 ERA in 84 innings during the regular season. Burke struck out 185 batters across 32 appearances (including 27 starts) and finished 17th among all pitchers in wins above replacement.

In addition to an explosive offense that was top 10 in both home runs and slugging percentage during the regular season, the White Sox have employed a unique pitching strategy, relying heavily on their relievers to throw multiple innings.

“We knew we had to be different,” general manager Chris Getz told MLB Network this month. “It became leaning into those arms. What’s the pathway to win? How do we solve today? Oftentimes it was getting creative with openers. Thankfully, we’ve got some arms that can go multiple innings.”

(It’s also possible the team’s success is coming from a higher power, as Pope Leo XIV is a fan. “I willingly invoke the Almighty’s abundant blessings upon you and your loved ones,” the pope wrote in a letter to the team in September.)
The man in charge of the dugout is Will Venable, who played in the majors from 2008 to 2016. Venable became Chicago’s manager in October 2024 and has become a key part of the franchise’s turnaround.

“For where the organization was and the pain of those couple years in which there was 100-loss seasons, to see the growth and have the fans be a part of this and be able to celebrate this, it makes me happy for everyone involved with White Sox baseball,” Venable said after the White Sox won in the wild-card round.

As impressive as the revival has been so far, the Sox don’t seem simply happy to be here. Asked in September what Chicago could do in the playoffs, designated hitter Andrew Benintendi told MLB.com his team was “confident.”
Added Benintendi: “We are dumb enough to think we can win it. So, why not?”

title: Sen. Ruben Gallego rolls out an economic agenda as he weighs a 2028 White House bid
summary: The Arizona Democrat told NBC News he’s “absolutely thinking about” running for president. He’s pitching a New Deal-style jobs program funded by data center and AI taxes.
story: WASHINGTON — Sen. Ruben Gallego, D-Ariz., who is eyeing a possible presidential bid in 2028, rolled out a new, national economic plan Wednesday that calls for boosting the minimum wage to $20 per hour and a New Deal-style public service jobs program funded by taxes on artificial intelligence companies and unpopular data centers.

In an interview with NBC News, Gallego said middle-class and working-class Americans are under assault due to rapidly advancing artificial intelligence and automation, as well as an economic system that has not sided with nor supported workers for a generation.

“There’s a lot of changes that are coming because of AI that we’re not prepared for. There’s been a lot of bad things that have been happening for the middle class for the last 40 years that we have not really changed, either. And that’s why I think you have this real anxiety out there that working America feels,” Gallego said in an interview Tuesday.

“I always felt like, you know, if I put 40 hours’ worth of honest work together, I would have enough to support my family, and then feel comfortable enough to go to a movie,” he continued. “That’s not happening anymore, and so that’s the most important focus of this plan.”

The November midterm elections are still weeks away, with both the House and Senate up for grabs, but Gallego’s decision to launch his AI and economic agenda now underscores just how quickly the political conversation will shift to what’s expected to be a crowded Democratic presidential contest.
Asked whether he plans to run in 2028, Gallego said he is considering it and trying to determine whether he can balance a grueling presidential bid with raising three young children.

“I’m not, you know, going to lie and say we’re not thinking about it. We are absolutely thinking about it,” said the 46-year-old senator, who was raised by a single mother and frequently talks about his up-from-the-bootstraps personal narrative.

He has “a young family,” he said, “so that has to be the most important thing. How do you balance running for that office, mind you, and, you know, still be an active father? That’s very difficult to do, and I have to have a family, you know, fully into that.”

But regardless of that decision, he emphasized that Democrats need to state what they stand for. “We want to make sure that people understand what I believe we should be focusing on starting in 2027 and going all the way through, whether I run for president or not,” he said.

Gallego’s detailed, 32-page plan, dubbed “Saving the Middle Class and Restoring the American Dream,” is a mix of dozens of populist ideas and pragmatic proposals. He divides it into five pillars: “Raise Wages and Improve Benefits,” “Create and Protect Quality Blue-Collar Jobs,” “Restore Worker Trust in Government in the Age of Artificial Intelligence,” “Expand Job-Creating Entrepreneurship, Focusing Outside of Superstar Cities,” and “Help Workers Find Jobs Faster.”
Amid recent warnings that AI could soon cause human extinction, Gallego’s proposals on AI and data centers are perhaps the timeliest.

He wants to establish a Franklin D. Roosevelt-style public service jobs program — funded by taxes on data centers and an excise tax on revenue from large AI companies — that would pay for jobs that “promote human connection and community cohesion.” Those could include coaching Little League; counseling people fighting addiction; beautifying neighborhoods; and caring for children, older adults, or sick or disabled people, according to the plan.

“My son’s Little League in Phoenix sometimes does not have enough coaches, does not have enough referees. There are leagues of that nature all around the country that we could be working with them to fully fund coaching programs, mentoring programs, childcare,” Gallego said. “We could pay people if they want to stay at home with their kids.”
For Subscribers

Gallego is also proposing allowing individuals to charge tech companies for using their personal data; imposing a “robot” tax to discourage corporations from shifting jobs away from humans; and requiring companies to have humans review AI or automated workplace decisions, including hiring or laying off employees.
For Subscribers

“Making sure that human bodies are more valuable to the workspace than robotic bodies,” he said, “because right now, the way that our tax policies are actually tilted, it’s actually tilted more for automation than for actually human people working in a workplace.”

Other ideas include tripling “union density,” or the percentage of workers in a particular industry in a union, by 2035; promoting “sectoral bargaining” to establish minimum labor standards across an entire industry; and requiring companies to pay double for overtime work rather than time and a half.

While many of his policy prescriptions are critical of President Donald Trump and his administration, Gallego also takes aim at his own party. At the conclusion of his proposal, he declares: “This bipartisan, failed status quo must end.”

Speaking to NBC News, Gallego said both parties share blame for the nation’s current problems. “I’m not saying that Democrats are worse than Republicans. I think on par, if you look at it, who has been worse for the working class in this country? It’s been Republicans, but Democrats can’t not be blamed in this,” he said.

“Corporations made massive amounts of money, shareholders made massive amounts of money, but the persons that basically started it all just got thrown to the side, right?” he continued. “And there should have been stronger negotiations led by Democrats during NAFTA and during all these trade deals that said, ‘You know what, we’ll have trade, but that wealth is going to be shared back down with the people that actually made us wealthy in the first place, these workers.’ We never went down that road.”

If he does mount a bid for president, Gallego’s past friendship with former Rep. Eric Swalwell, D-Calif., who resigned this year amid sexual assault allegations, could become a liability. Swalwell denied any sexual misconduct, and Gallego said he was not aware of inappropriate behavior by his then-friend.
Asked if that will be a distraction going forward, Gallego said the issue has already been heavily scrutinized.

“I think we’ve been extremely scrutinized ... by the press. They’ve turned over every leaf and every aspect of my life. You know, they had an Ethics Committee that also looked into it, and everything’s come out, you know, clean,” Gallego said.

The Senate Ethics Committee dismissed a complaint against Gallego, brought by Republican Rep. Anna Paulina Luna of Florida, saying it found no evidence of inappropriate sexual conduct or a campaign finance violation.

“We’ve been focusing on good work and campaigning all across the country for Democrats. ... People have seen the value that I bring to the Democratic Party. ... And as long as I continue to really lean in with forward-leaning policies that are really calling to what America needs right now,” he said, “that’s going to be the biggest determination of my future.”

title: Florida poll: Republicans lead in the races for governor and Senate
summary: The new survey shows the state’s Hispanic voters shifting away from President Donald Trump after Republicans made gains in 2024.
story: Republican Byron Donalds holds a 7-percentage-point advantage over Democrat David Jolly in the Florida governor’s race, according to a new NBC South Florida/Telemundo Station Group poll, while Republican Sen. Ashley Moody is up by 10 points in her matchup against Democratic challenger Angie Nixon.

Donalds, a congressman from the southwest corner of the state, is at 48% in the poll, compared with Jolly’s 41%, in a race in which Donalds has had a commanding financial advantage. (That advantage is just inside the poll’s margin of error, but Donalds has the edge in most of the range of possibilities.)

Moody is at 50% in the Senate race, compared with 40% for Nixon, a Democratic Socialists of America-aligned candidate who got into the general election after a surprise primary victory over Democrat Alexander Vindman in August.

The results come amid broad Democratic optimism about the 2026 elections, with public polling showing the party making races in some typically red states into competitive contests this year. This poll suggests limits to that apparent momentum in other places.

The poll also took a snapshot of the state’s hugely influential bloc of Hispanic voters, largely congregated in South Florida. In 2024, Donald Trump won Hispanic-heavy Miami-Dade County by roughly 11 points, a significant reversal in a part of the state that had long been Democratic-leaning. Joe Biden won the county by 7 points in 2020.

But now, Florida Hispanic voters — including large Cuban, Nicaraguan, Honduran and Colombian populations — appear to be swinging back away from Trump, even as other high-profile Republican candidates hold comfortable leads among Hispanic voters.

Donalds holds a 48%-43% lead over Jolly among Hispanic voters, according to the survey, while Moody is up 47%-40% over Nixon. Trump’s job performance rating, however, is underwater, with 49% disapproving of his job performance, compared with 45% who approve.
For Subscribers
Overall, 48% of all Florida likely voters approve of Trump’s job performance and 48% disapprove.

Before Trump’s gains among Florida’s Hispanic population in 2024, Democrats had generally won the demographic in the state by comfortable margins. Democrats argue that recent special election victories in Florida show the party has already started winning back the Hispanic vote, in part because of Trump’s aggressive immigration enforcement policy. Unhappiness with prices and the cost of living has also affected Trump’s ratings among Hispanic voters.

“In legislative races in Florida, we have seen huge swings,” Suzan DelBene, D-Wash., chair of the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee, told NBC News last week, speaking of the committee’s efforts in Florida House races. She said that on immigration, Trump and his party broke a promise “to go after the worst of the worst.”
For Subscribers

By far the most important issue identified was inflation and the cost of living, with 30% saying it is likeliest to influence their votes. In both the overall sample and the sample of Hispanic voters, “direction of the state or country” (17%) was the second most important issue. The broader polling data put “immigration enforcement” as the third most important issue (16%), while the Hispanic sample put property taxes (13%) as the third most important issue. Immigration enforcement was the fourth most important issue among Hispanic voters (12%).
Questions about the Trump administration’s push to allow local and state policy to cooperate with federal immigration officials fell along party lines.
Among all voters, 85% of Republicans support the policy, compared with 18% of Democrats and 44% of those identified as independent voters who supported the harsher immigration enforcement tactics.
Property taxes have also been front and center in Florida during the midterms.

The state Republican Party and term-limited Gov. Ron DeSantis support a ballot measure, known as Amendment 3, that would increase property tax exemptions to the first $250,000 of a home’s value by 2028. The exemption cap is currently $50,000.

In the poll of all Florida voters, 55% back the amendment, 26% oppose it, and 19% are undecided. Nearly three-quarters (74%) of Republicans supported the idea, compared with 36% for Democrats and 43% for independents.

The overall survey questioned 625 registered voters, all of whom said they were likely to vote in the November elections. They were interviewed over the telephone by Mason-Dixon Polling & Research Inc. from Sept. 28 to Thursday, with a margin of error of plus or minus 4 percentage points. The same time frame and methods were used to survey 400 Hispanic registered voters, with a margin of error of plus or minus 5 percentage points.

Best overall October Prime Day deals
Premier Protein Shake, Chocolate (12 Pack)

Premier Protein’s shakes are ideal for snacking on the go. Each one has 30 grams of protein, no added sugar and 160 calories, according to the brand, plus they’re gluten-free. They come in over a dozen creamy flavors, like chocolate, vanilla, cookies and cream, cafe latte and pumpkin spice, almost all of which are currently on sale.
Dawn Platinum Powerwash Dish Spray Bundle

I’m very picky about dish soap because I don’t have a dishwasher, and out of all the options I’ve tested, Dawn Powerwash Spray is hands-down the best one. It easily removes dirt and grime from my dishes without pre-soaking, and it leaves them literally sparkling. Also, since the soap works without water, I don’t turn my faucet on until I’m ready to rinse. Beyond washing dishes, you can use Dawn’s spray on laundry stains, kitchen surfaces, appliances and grills, according to the brand. This starter kit comes with four bottles of liquid and one reusable sprayer head.
iRobot Roomba 115X Combo Robot Vacuum & Mop

This robot vacuum suctions up dirt and debris, and it has a built-in mop that scrubs floors to leave them shiny. It’s designed with sensors that map your home to detect and avoid obstacles, and it connects to the Roomba Home app so you can select cleaning modes, create cleaning schedules, adjust suction level and more. You can also set keep-out and no-mop zones where needed, like on area rugs. The appliance comes with a charging dock, reusable microfiber mopping pad and edge sweeping brush.
Samsonite Freeform 2-Piece Luggage Set

I’ve beat up my Samsonite luggage while traveling over the years, but it still works perfectly, looks great and, perhaps most importantly, fits all my stuff. You get a matching expandable carry-on and checked bag with this set, both of which are lightweight and made with hard, protective exteriors. The suitcases have spacious interiors with elastic straps, a divider and a pouch for organization, plus they’re designed with smoothly gliding wheels, a built-in ID tag, a height-adjustable handle and a TSA-approved lock.
Anker Nano Power Bank

Never worry about a dead phone or earbuds again with Anker’s Nano Power Bank, which has a built-in folding USB-C connector, eliminating the need for a cable. It fits in the palm of your hand and weighs 3.5 ounces, so you can put it in any bag or even your pocket. The Nano comes with a charging cable when you need to refill its battery, or you can connect it directly to a block.
Cascade Platinum Plus Dishwasher Pods

The most boring essentials on your shopping list are often the best deals to take advantage of during Prime Big Deal Days — you’ll need to restock eventually, so you might as well do it when items are discounted. Cascade’s dishwasher pods are a perfect example. They come in a pack of 62, and with the discount applied, you’re only paying about 0.28 per pod. Each one has soap inside that gets rid of grease and food residue, and it cleans your dishwasher’s filter, too.
Amazon Smart Plug

Once you connect devices like lamps, fans and small kitchen appliances to the Amazon Smart Plug, you can control them through an app or via voice commands. The app also lets you set timers, schedules and routines — for example, I connect my Christmas lights to this smart plug and create a schedule for them so they turn on at 10 a.m. and turn off at 10 p.m. The plug is compact to keep your second outlet free.
Shark Navigator Lift-Away Upright Vacuum (NV352)

I rely on this corded vacuum to get rid of dirt, dust and hair on hard floors and carpets in my three-pet home. It has powerful suction, a multi-stage washable HEPA filter to trap allergens and a swivel steering system that makes it easy to navigate. My favorite part of the vacuum is the detachable pod, which I carry around my home and use the extended reach tool to clean above door frames, under furniture and on stairs. Interchangeable wide upholstery and crevice attachments for the extended reach tool are included.
Apple AirPods Pro 3

Apple’s AirPods Pro 3 made our list of the best earbuds, and I use mine every day while listening to music on runs, taking calls and blocking out noisy city streets. They’re comfortable and secure in my ears even when I get sweaty — they come with five interchangeable ear tips so you can find the right fit. The AirPods have three listening modes, including active noise cancellation, hours of battery life with the included charging case and advanced features like heart rate sensing during workouts, hearing aid mode and live language translation.
Medicube Toner Pads

Exfoliating with Medicube’s Zero Pore Pads every other night has transformed my skin in the past year. The pads are soaked in a serum made with AHAs and BHAs, ingredients that have made my skin noticeably softer, smoother and clearer. There’s two sides to the pads: you use the textured one first to remove dead skin cells, then the soft one to soothe. The pads come with a tweezer, preventing you from touching those inside the container with dirty hands.
Waterpik Cordless Advanced 2.0 Flosser

If you’re not a fan of thread floss or floss pickers, using a water flosser is another way to get rid of plaque. This one is a NBC Selected Wellness Award winner with three pressure settings and a rechargeable battery that lasts up to four weeks, according to the brand. It comes with four interchangeable tips that rotate 360 degrees, letting you reach all parts of your mouth, and the built-in reservoir on its handle holds enough water for a 45-second clean.
Amazon Kindle Paperwhite Signature Edition 32GB

We named the Paperwhite Amazon’s best Kindle because of its extra-long battery life that lasts up to 12 weeks. It also has a front light that automatically adjusts depending on your environment, helping you see the glare-free screen clearly. The Kindle Paperwhite is water-resistant, and you can charge it via the USB-C port or wirelessly with a charging dock that’s sold separately.
LifeStraw Personal Water Filter

Take LifeStraw’s Personal Water Filter on hikes and camping trips, or put it in your emergency kit. You use it like a straw, and its built-in filter removes over 99 percent of bacteria, parasites and microplastics from water, according to the brand. You can use it to filter up to 1,000 gallons of water before needing a new one.
Yeti Rambler 35-oz. Straw Mug 2.0
Lowest price ever

Keep beverages cold and ice frozen all day with this dishwasher-safe water bottle, which has a handle, a straw lid and a stainless steel, double-wall vacuum insulated design. It’s also cupholder-compatible.
Wavytalk Red Light Therapy Mask

Wavytalk’s red light therapy mask uses different light modes to target fine lines, acne and skin tone, with enhanced light delivery in the T- and U-zones to address those common problem areas, according to the brand. It fully covers your face to prevent itchiness or missed spots, and it’s made from a soft silicone material with adjustable head straps. You can choose from 10-, 15- or 20-minute sessions.
October Prime Day deals on household essentials and groceries
Hefty Ultra Strong 13-Gallon Trash Bags

These trash bags are multi-layered and slightly stretchy to prevent leaks and rips while you fill them to the brim, and they have a drawstring closure to keep everything inside once full. They’re also made with baking soda and added fragrance to neutralize odors. You get 80 13-gallon bags in this pack.
Energizer AA and AAA Batteries (48 Count)
I always buy batteries when they’re on sale so I never run out at home. This pack comes with 24 AAs and 24 AAAs, and they last for up to 10 years in storage, according to the brand.
Tide Odor + Oxi Laundry Detergent Pods 63-pack

These Tide Pods don’t just clean clothes. The detergent inside each one also fights odors, pre-treats and removes stains, protects colors and boosts scents, according to the brand. I use them for all my laundry, including sweaty workout clothes and my pets’ beds, and I’ve never had an issue with them not dissolving, even in cold water. You get 63 Tide Pods in this pack, which come in a resealable container.
Scrub Daddy Scrub Mommy Sponges

The dual-sided Scrub Mommy is the only sponge I buy. Its scrubber side is soft in warm water yet firm in cold water to get rid of stuck-on grime, while its sponge side is always soft and highly absorbent to create suds. The circular sponges are easy to hold, and the smiley face in the center is purposeful: You can put your fingers in the eyes for a secure grip and put utensils through the mouth to wipe them down. The Scrub Mommy is odor-resistant, scratch-free and dishwasher-safe.
October Prime Day beauty and wellness deals
Olay Regenerist Face Moisturizer

This moisturizer is formulated with ingredients like collagen peptides, niacinamide and vitamin B5 to strengthen the skin barrier, add hydration and improve the appearance of wrinkles so your skin is smoother and firmer over time, according to the brand. You can use it in the morning and at night, plus it’s fragrance-free.
Grace & Stella Under Eye Patches Variety Pack

I wear these under eye patches almost every day to depuff the area under my eyes before putting on my makeup or after taking it off. They’re made from a cooling gel material and soaked in serum made from ingredients to target different concerns, like vitamin C for brightening and peptides for moisturizing. The masks come individually packed, and this set comes with 18 pairs across six types: brightening, restoring, firming, illuminating, energizing and moisturizing.
Colgate Optic White Pro Series High Impact White Toothpaste (3 Pack)

Colgate’s toothpaste is made with 5 percent hydrogen peroxide, a bleaching ingredient that helps remove stains from teeth and make your smile less yellow. There’s also cavity-fighting fluoride in its formula. The minty whitening toothpaste is safe for daily use and doesn’t cause tooth sensitivity, according to the brand.
Biodance Bio-Collagen Real Deep Mask

When you leave this sheet mask on for three to four hours, or overnight, it turns transparent as your skin absorbs the serum it’s soaked in. It’s made with ingredients like hyaluronic acid and niacinamide to hydrate, refine enlarged pores, improve skin elasticity, brighten tone and smooth fine lines and wrinkles, according to the brand. You get four masks in this pack, and they’re each individually wrapped.
Crest 3D Whitestrips

Editor’s note: This product dropped to $34.99 for a few days in August, but because it’s over 20% off, highly rated and a NBC Selected editor- and reader- favorite product, we still recommend the deal.

Out of all the teeth whitening strips I’ve tested, Crest’s are the most effective and easiest to apply, plus they’re comfortable and stay in place — they’re so thin that I can have full conversations while wearing them. Each strip is coated in hydrogen peroxide, a bleaching ingredient that removes stains and brightens your smile, according to the brand. You get enough strips for 22 45-minute treatments with this pack.
Laneige Lip Glowy Balm

Laneige’s lip balm gives my lips a sheer tint and a glossy finish while moisturizing them with ingredients like shea and murumuru seed butters. It keeps my lips softer throughout the day and feels lightweight. I wear it on its own, and I often layer it over matte lipstick.
Amika Perk Up Plus Dry Shampoo

Amika’s dry shampoo came highly recommended to us by numerous hair stylists. They say the rice starch in its formula effectively absorbs moisture from the scalp and reduces odors to extend time between washes, while sea buckthorn berry nourishes the hair. It also blends into hair easily, is lightweight and adds volume and body.
Shark DePuffi

The internet-famous Shark DePuffi is currently on sale for the first time ever, so don’t wait any longer to get your hands on it. The skin care device has six customizable temperatures that go from cold to hot, and it’s made with a gua sha-inspired edge — as you massage it along your face and neck to encourage lymphatic flow, it depuffs, sculpts and temporarily relieves muscle tension, according to the brand. You get a travel case and charger with your purchase.
Philips Sonicare 5950 Electric Toothbrush

Philips Sonicare’s 5950 Electric Toothbrush has all the features dentists told us to look for while shopping: a pressure sensor, a timer, a brush head replacement reminder and adjustable brushing settings. Its battery lasts for about 21 days before you need to recharge it, and it comes with a travel case and charging stand.
October Prime Day home deals
Ugg Adalee Throw Blanket

Prepare for the cozy season ahead by adding Ugg’s faux fur blanket to your couch or bed. It’s double-sided, so it feels soft against your skin no matter how you use it, and it’s roomy enough for two people to share. While Ugg recommends dry cleaning the blanket, you can also machine wash it on cold, according to the brand.
Casper Sleep Original Pillow

The Casper Sleep Original Pillow is a NBC Selected staff-favorite product, and many of us rest our heads on it every night. It’s stuffed with a down alternative material, has a breathable cotton cover and gets its medium-soft feel from a two-layer design: the inner layer is firmer to offer support, while outer layer is plush for extra comfort. The pillow is machine-washable and clump-resistant.
Bissell Little Green Multi-Purpose Portable Carpet and Upholstery Cleaner

I firmly believe that every home should have a Bissell Little Green machine due to how many times mine has saved carpets and upholstered furniture that would have otherwise been unsalvageable. You fill one of the tanks with a cleaning solution and use the nozzle to spray the mess, scrub it and suction it up. The dirty solution goes into a separate tank, which you remove when you’re done to pour the liquid down the drain. The appliance comes with a self-cleaning attachment, a stain tool, a crevice tool and cleaning solution concentrate.
Hoto 25-Piece Electric Screwdriver Kit

Hoto’s rechargeable electric screwdriver helps you build and fix stuff at home (or on the go) much faster than a standard tool. It comes with 25 interchangeable bits, and it has three adjustable torque settings and a built-in LED light to provide clear visibility. The screwdriver comes with a case to keep all the pieces organized.
Magna-Tiles MicroMags Deluxe Magnetic Construction Set

I’ve never met a kid who doesn’t love Magna-Tiles, and if I’m being honest, I enjoy using them, too. This set comes with 70 magnetic blocks in a rainbow of colors and different shapes like rectangles, triangles and squares. In addition to letting kids be creative while building, the brand says the blocks help with hand-eye coordination and fine motor skills.
October Prime Day kitchen deals
KitchenAid Ribbed Soft Silicone Oven Mitt (2-Pack)

These were one of my best purchases during last year’s Prime Big Deal Days. Their ribbed silicone exterior helps me grip hot pots and pans, and they’re heat-resistant up to 500 degrees Fahrenheit, according to the brand. The material is also water-resistant, so I don’t worry about spills or splashes. The inside of the mitts are lined with cotton, making them soft against my skin.
Ecolution Micro-Pop

You can make your own fresh popcorn at home with this kitchen gadget. Use the built-in measuring cup on the lid to portion out kernels, pour them into the popper and microwave it for about three minutes. You can also put butter on the lid, which has holes that let it melt onto the popcorn. Plus, once your snack is done cooking, you can use the popper as a serving bowl.
Stasher Reusable Silicone Storage Bags

I traded disposable plastic bags for Stasher’s reusable silicone bags years ago. I use them every day to pack my lunch and store ingredients at home. The bags have air-tight, leak-free seals, and they’re freezer-, microwave-, dishwasher- and oven-safe up to 425 degrees Fahrenheit, according Stasher. You can also use them for sous-vide cooking, as well as write on them with dry-erase markers for easy labeling. This pack comes with four bags in different sizes: snack, sandwich, stand-up mid and 2-cup bowl.
Keurig K-Express Single Serve K-Cup Pod Coffee Maker

This single-serve coffee maker brews an 8-, 10- or 12-ounce cup in less than a minute. It has a strong brew setting if you like your coffee extra flavorful, and it’s designed with a 42-ounce removable water reservoir that’s easy to refill. The machine is compact, making it ideal for small spaces, and you can remove the drip tray to fit tall travel mugs.
October Prime Day tech deals
Blink Battery Doorbell 2K+

You can monitor visitors and deliveries at all times with Blink’s video doorbell. It connects to the brand’s app, letting you livestream head-to-toe video (including in night vision) and audio, as well as speak to people. The doorbell runs on two AA batteries, comes with a mounting kit and you can install it wire-free. There’s also a Blink subscription available for an additional fee, which gives you access to features like in-app person detection and motion-activated notifications.
Amazon Fire TV Stick HD

Turn any TV into a smart TV with Amazon’s Fire Stick, which you simply plug into an HDMI port to use. It lets you stream entertainment from your favorite platforms and watch live TV in HD. The Fire Stick comes with a remote that lets you control the TV via buttons or voice commands. It’s also compact so it won’t block other ports.
Life360 Tile Mate

Attach this device to your keys, slip it inside a pocket or put it on a carabiner clip to find where your items are. The tracker connects to the Life360 app, letting you see its location, ring it and share information with loved ones. You can also press the tracker’s built-in button to ring your phone or send an SOS alert. The brand says its battery lasts up to three years.
She’s Birdie Personal Safety Alarm

If you’re in an emergency, you pull up the top ring on the She’s Birdie safety keychain to activate its loud alarm and strobe light to attract help. To stop the alarm, just push the ring back in. October Prime Day ends at 11:59 p.m. PT on October 7 —  that’s October 8 at 2:59 a.m. ET, 1:59 a.m. CT and 12:59 a.m. MT.

Amazon doesn’t have a Prime Day-specific return policy. You can return most Amazon purchases within 30 days of delivery and get your money back as long as they’re in original or unused condition. There are exceptions, however, so read the fine print before buying anything.

The best deals on October Prime Day usually center around Amazon-owned technology like Echo, Fire, Blink and Ring devices, small home and kitchen appliances, beauty products, household basics and groceries. Products across all categories are generally cheaper on October Prime Day, with many brands discounting products by over 20 percent. Prices on tech, household essentials and groceries, small home and kitchen appliances, beauty products, giftable items and holiday decor tend to drop the most overall.

Yes, October Prime Day is actually worth it, so long as you shop strategically. The sale offers some of the lowest prices of the year on products across categories, giving you a chance to start shopping for holiday gifts, upgrade outdated or broken items and restock your favorite basics, like skin care, cleaning supplies and groceries. But ultimately, deals are only worth it if you actually need something, so plan your spending to prevent making impulse purchases.

Vital Proteins Collagen Peptides Powder

Mix this collagen powder into either hot and cold beverages, including water, smoothies, coffee and tea. It has collagen sourced from grass-fed, pasture-raised bovine, vitamin C and hyaluronic acid to keep bones, joints, nails and hair healthy, according to the brand.
