title: U.S. monitors suspected Russian plague case as Trump plans call with Putin
summary: Trump has said the U.S. is willing to help Russia, where the death of a staffer at an anti-plague lab has sparked global public health concerns.
story: President Donald Trump said Tuesday that he has a call scheduled with Russian President Vladimir Putin to discuss the pneumonic plague, after the death of a female staffer at a Russian anti-plague lab that’s sparked public health fears worldwide.
Asked whether he had spoken with Putin about the matter, Trump told reporters on the White House South Lawn that he had a “call scheduled” and that it would take place “very soon.”
On Wednesday, the Kremlin’s spokesman Dmitry Peskov denied a call had been set up, saying “no substantive arrangements have been made.”
Trump had told reporters Monday that he was willing to help Russia, calling the pneumonic plague “a rough disease.”
“I hate to see them having it,” Trump said. “Anybody that has that kind of a problem, we’re always willing to help.”
A Russian health watchdog said last week that a female staffer at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Institute of Siberia and the Far East, had died from a “pneumonia of undetermined” origin.
The woman’s mother spoke with Russian media, which identified her as Darya Shipilova.
The watchdog said that plague was not found among the staffer’s contacts tested so far, saying only that they found two cases of Covid and two of rhinovirus.
The U.S. and the World Health Organization have been leading the call for more transparency from Russia in the wake of Shipilova’s death.

“Timely, complete and transparent information sharing under the International Health Regulations is essential to clarify conflicting reports and enable an accurate assessment of potential public health risks,” WHO Director-General Dr. Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said in a statement Tuesday.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

Earlier, the agency said Russian health officials had told it that a case of plague had not been recorded in Irkutsk. It was still waiting for information on the exact pneumonia-causing pathogen that may have led to Shipilova’s death, it added.

A State Department official told NBC News earlier Tuesday that the U.S. had been in contact with the Russian government regarding the incident since as early as Friday, following reports of Shipilova’s death.
It is “incumbent upon Russia to obviously share more information with the world,” Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Tuesday.

“Maybe, you know, there’s nothing there. Maybe it’s bigger than we thought. We don’t know,” Rubio told reporters during a news conference in Iceland. “But I think it would be reckless at this moment, given the limited information we still have, to speculate about what this might or might not be or what this is or what this isn’t.”

The U.S. embassy in Russia issued a health alert Tuesday, saying it was following the situation closely and urging Americans in the Irkutsk region to follow guidance of local health authorities, avoid affected facilities and seek medical care promptly if they develop fever or respiratory symptoms.
“The U.S. government has limited ability to help U.S. citizens in Russia, especially outside of Moscow,” the embassy said.

The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention said Tuesday it was aware of and monitoring reports of the death, which it called “a suspected case of pneumonic plague in the Irkutsk region of Russia.”

“At this time, there is no indication of a broader threat to the United States, but CDC and our interagency partners are prepared and will continue to monitor the situation closely,” the CDC wrote on X.

title: Sen. Ruben Gallego rolls out an economic agenda as he weighs a 2028 White House bid
summary: The Arizona Democrat told NBC News he’s “absolutely thinking about” running for president. He’s pitching a New Deal-style jobs program funded by data center and AI taxes.
story: WASHINGTON — Sen. Ruben Gallego, D-Ariz., who is eyeing a possible presidential bid in 2028, rolled out a new, national economic plan Wednesday that calls for boosting the minimum wage to $20 per hour and a New Deal-style public service jobs program funded by taxes on artificial intelligence companies and unpopular data centers.

In an interview with NBC News, Gallego said middle-class and working-class Americans are under assault due to rapidly advancing artificial intelligence and automation, as well as an economic system that has not sided with nor supported workers for a generation.

“There’s a lot of changes that are coming because of AI that we’re not prepared for. There’s been a lot of bad things that have been happening for the middle class for the last 40 years that we have not really changed, either. And that’s why I think you have this real anxiety out there that working America feels,” Gallego said in an interview Tuesday.

“I always felt like, you know, if I put 40 hours’ worth of honest work together, I would have enough to support my family, and then feel comfortable enough to go to a movie,” he continued. “That’s not happening anymore, and so that’s the most important focus of this plan.”

The November midterm elections are still weeks away, with both the House and Senate up for grabs, but Gallego’s decision to launch his AI and economic agenda now underscores just how quickly the political conversation will shift to what’s expected to be a crowded Democratic presidential contest.
Asked whether he plans to run in 2028, Gallego said he is considering it and trying to determine whether he can balance a grueling presidential bid with raising three young children.

“I’m not, you know, going to lie and say we’re not thinking about it. We are absolutely thinking about it,” said the 46-year-old senator, who was raised by a single mother and frequently talks about his up-from-the-bootstraps personal narrative.

He has “a young family,” he said, “so that has to be the most important thing. How do you balance running for that office, mind you, and, you know, still be an active father? That’s very difficult to do, and I have to have a family, you know, fully into that.”

But regardless of that decision, he emphasized that Democrats need to state what they stand for. “We want to make sure that people understand what I believe we should be focusing on starting in 2027 and going all the way through, whether I run for president or not,” he said.

Gallego’s detailed, 32-page plan, dubbed “Saving the Middle Class and Restoring the American Dream,” is a mix of dozens of populist ideas and pragmatic proposals. He divides it into five pillars: “Raise Wages and Improve Benefits,” “Create and Protect Quality Blue-Collar Jobs,” “Restore Worker Trust in Government in the Age of Artificial Intelligence,” “Expand Job-Creating Entrepreneurship, Focusing Outside of Superstar Cities,” and “Help Workers Find Jobs Faster.”
Amid recent warnings that AI could soon cause human extinction, Gallego’s proposals on AI and data centers are perhaps the timeliest.

He wants to establish a Franklin D. Roosevelt-style public service jobs program — funded by taxes on data centers and an excise tax on revenue from large AI companies — that would pay for jobs that “promote human connection and community cohesion.” Those could include coaching Little League; counseling people fighting addiction; beautifying neighborhoods; and caring for children, older adults, or sick or disabled people, according to the plan.

“My son’s Little League in Phoenix sometimes does not have enough coaches, does not have enough referees. There are leagues of that nature all around the country that we could be working with them to fully fund coaching programs, mentoring programs, childcare,” Gallego said. “We could pay people if they want to stay at home with their kids.”
For Subscribers

Gallego is also proposing allowing individuals to charge tech companies for using their personal data; imposing a “robot” tax to discourage corporations from shifting jobs away from humans; and requiring companies to have humans review AI or automated workplace decisions, including hiring or laying off employees.
For Subscribers

“Making sure that human bodies are more valuable to the workspace than robotic bodies,” he said, “because right now, the way that our tax policies are actually tilted, it’s actually tilted more for automation than for actually human people working in a workplace.”

Other ideas include tripling “union density,” or the percentage of workers in a particular industry in a union, by 2035; promoting “sectoral bargaining” to establish minimum labor standards across an entire industry; and requiring companies to pay double for overtime work rather than time and a half.

While many of his policy prescriptions are critical of President Donald Trump and his administration, Gallego also takes aim at his own party. At the conclusion of his proposal, he declares: “This bipartisan, failed status quo must end.”

Speaking to NBC News, Gallego said both parties share blame for the nation’s current problems. “I’m not saying that Democrats are worse than Republicans. I think on par, if you look at it, who has been worse for the working class in this country? It’s been Republicans, but Democrats can’t not be blamed in this,” he said.

“Corporations made massive amounts of money, shareholders made massive amounts of money, but the persons that basically started it all just got thrown to the side, right?” he continued. “And there should have been stronger negotiations led by Democrats during NAFTA and during all these trade deals that said, ‘You know what, we’ll have trade, but that wealth is going to be shared back down with the people that actually made us wealthy in the first place, these workers.’ We never went down that road.”

If he does mount a bid for president, Gallego’s past friendship with former Rep. Eric Swalwell, D-Calif., who resigned this year amid sexual assault allegations, could become a liability. Swalwell denied any sexual misconduct, and Gallego said he was not aware of inappropriate behavior by his then-friend.
Asked if that will be a distraction going forward, Gallego said the issue has already been heavily scrutinized.

“I think we’ve been extremely scrutinized ... by the press. They’ve turned over every leaf and every aspect of my life. You know, they had an Ethics Committee that also looked into it, and everything’s come out, you know, clean,” Gallego said.

The Senate Ethics Committee dismissed a complaint against Gallego, brought by Republican Rep. Anna Paulina Luna of Florida, saying it found no evidence of inappropriate sexual conduct or a campaign finance violation.

“We’ve been focusing on good work and campaigning all across the country for Democrats. ... People have seen the value that I bring to the Democratic Party. ... And as long as I continue to really lean in with forward-leaning policies that are really calling to what America needs right now,” he said, “that’s going to be the biggest determination of my future.”

title: CIA officer arrested with gold bars admits he exposed secret intelligence source to a foreign official
summary: David Rush, who was fired, pleaded guilty to one count of wire fraud and will be sentenced Jan. 28.
story: ALEXANDRIA, Va. — A high-ranking CIA officer arrested after federal agents found roughly 600 pounds of gold bars stashed in his home also disclosed details about a secret U.S. intelligence source to a foreign official, prosecutors said Tuesday during his plea hearing.
David Rush, 49, admitted to one count of wire fraud under an agreement with federal prosecutors and faces up to 20 years in prison when he is sentenced Jan. 28.

Justice Department officials said Rush siphoned off $194 million in government funds, using his position at the CIA to create an elaborate scheme designed to facilitate his “maximum self-enrichment at the expense of the United States.”

In a plea document, Rush admitted that in late 2025 he disclosed “certain descriptive information of a U.S. government clandestine human source” that could “endanger the safety and life of the human source and the U.S. government officers working with the source,” as well as jeopardize America’s “ability to recruit human sources, who rely on the U.S. government’s assurance of absolute secrecy.”
Lawyers for Rush declined to comment.
Rush has been in jail since his arrest May 19, after investigators said he made up details about his education and military service record, fooling the nation’s top spy agency for years.

As a top officer at the CIA’s Directorate of Science and Technology, Rush had access to the nation’s most secret programs — and he used that to his benefit, prosecutors said. Rush worked as a liaison to the Defense Department for sensitive military programs and collaborated closely with its powerful second in command, Steve Feinberg, people familiar with the work have told NBC News.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

The case has prompted a wave of shock and anxiety among lawmakers and within the insular spy agency. How could someone have fooled the highest levels of government for decades, and how could he have gotten through what is considered a rigorous vetting process to join the CIA? The intelligence community’s watchdog is separately investigating, according to a U.S. official and a person familiar with the probe.
More on the David Rush case

CIA officer accused of stealing gold bars was no low-level agentCIA officer arrested with gold bars worked on Pentagon’s nuclear sub program, sources sayBefore arrest with 303 gold bars, CIA officer spun tale he was Top Gun fighter pilotCIA officer’s arrest with 303 gold bars thrusts the Pentagon’s No. 2 into an unwelcome spotlight
CIA officer accused of stealing gold bars was no low-level agent
CIA officer arrested with gold bars worked on Pentagon’s nuclear sub program, sources say
Before arrest with 303 gold bars, CIA officer spun tale he was Top Gun fighter pilot
CIA officer’s arrest with 303 gold bars thrusts the Pentagon’s No. 2 into an unwelcome spotlight

Until Tuesday, Rush — who was placed on leave sometime before his arrest and then fired — had only formally been charged with one count of theft of public funds, accused of falsifying his pay records. His court case was postponed for weeks as his lawyers and the government worked toward a possible plea agreement. U.S. District Judge Michael Nachmanoff approved the plea deal Tuesday.

Rush acted alone, using his manufactured bona fides to create confidence in his work, court documents say. No other CIA officials, government employees or contractors were accused of crimes in the case. According to court documents, his deceptions “caused contractors and subcontractors to carry out the transactions.”

Rush fabricated a highly classified program to funnel tens of millions of dollars for his personal purchase of luxury real estate in Florida and invented a sensitive government “activity” to acquire the gold bars.
“Rush effectively acted as his own approving official, enabling him to expend substantial amounts of United States government money without meaningful scrutiny,” according to court documents.

During their search of his home, investigators seized about 300 gold bars, federal officials said, along with about $2 million in U.S. currency and 35 luxury watches. Initially, investigators said it was 303 bars, but on Tuesday revised that figure to 298 bars.
The gold was for what Rush claimed was an official work purpose, and he had said that they were distributed out — the spy agency uses all sorts of unusual methods in its work.

Rush, according to federal prosecutors, also fabricated a classified special access program, and told associates he needed luxury real estate in South Florida for it. He had $145 million transferred to a holding company for four luxury properties and vehicles.
He lied to associates, telling them that highly placed government officials knew about the need for the real estate and approved the transaction.
Rush also spent $1.8 million of the government’s money for private charter flights, but a CIA review later found he had “no legitimate official requirement” for the flights, prosecutors said.
The interstate wire fraud occurred in January — when Rush caused a government employee to send $45 million for his scheme, prosecutors said.

The case also has cast a spotlight on Rush’s relationship with Feinberg, as NBC News reported. The FBI reviewed video showing Rush and Feinberg at a residence in the Washington region that is linked to the federal government, according to four people familiar with the video.

Feinberg has been interviewed by the FBI, according to two people familiar with the investigation, but has not been accused of any wrongdoing, and the bureau said he is not under investigation. There’s no indication that Feinberg knew of Rush’s alleged fabrications. A Pentagon spokesman has said Feinberg and Rush were not close.

CIA Director John Ratcliffe said in a statement Tuesday that the agency “immediately” referred the case to the FBI after an internal investigation identified potential crimes. He said Rush “abused his position and betrayed the public trust and should be held fully accountable for his actions.”

FBI Director Kash Patel said in a statement that Rush “betrayed his oath, his co-workers, and the American people” when he “defrauded the government of hundreds of millions of dollars, and then misused those funds for extravagant purchases.”

title: Jeremy Allen White Reveals If He’d Want to Play Gene Wilder In Upcoming Biopic
summary: Jeremy Allen White has often drawn comparisons to the legendary Gene Wilder. He answers if he’d want to play the actor in a biopic.
story: Between his magnetic screen presence and curly blond hair, Jeremy Allen White has often drawn comparisons to the legendary Gene Wilder.

“The Bear” star does not shy away from it, even if it means potentially accepting the intimidating task of playing the iconic “Young Frankenstein” and “Willy Wonka & the Chocolate Factory” actor onscreen.

A biopic of Wilder is in the works, but there has been no announcement yet of who will play him, according to Deadline. White, 35, was asked by Craig Melvin on TODAY Oct. 7 if he would be interested in the role.

“Absolutely, it would be my honor,” White said. “‘Young Frankenstein’ is one of my earliest film memories. ‘Blazing Saddles’ — he was a genius, it would be an honor. I love him, I’ve always loved him. I need the call.”
White so strikingly resembles a young Wilder that it’s become a meme online. He noted in a 2024 interview with Buzzfeed that the two have no relation.
“I’m not related to Gene Wilder,” White said. “I think a lot of people think I am.”
Director Dito Montiel and writer Jeremy Roth are set to create the  Wilder biopic, Deadline reported in June. Wilder died at 83 in 2016.

White revealing that he would welcome the role came after his reflections on the weight that comes with portraying real-life figures. He played a young Bruce Springsteen in the 2025 film “Deliver Me From Nowhere.”
“It was a wonderful experience, but it was a tremendous amount of pressure,” White said on TODAY about playing The Boss.
The actor admittedly had “a little hesitation” about his latest role in “The Social Reckoning” because he’s playing another real person. He stars as former Wall Street Journal reporter Jeff Horwitz.

“I think I was just anxious about the idea of going ahead and playing another real person right away and feeling that responsibility again,” he said. “I think I wanted my next thing to be something that was just my own and my own kind of creation and to feel no pressure to do any kind of impersonation.”
But it was “The Social Reckoning” director Aaron Sorkin who put White at ease.

“Learn as much as you can, read his book, watch interviews, but don’t feel like you have to do any kind of mimicry,” White recalled of Sorkin’s guidance. “Make it your own. So it was kind of the best of both worlds.”

title: ‘Heated Rivalry’ Annotated Scripts Reveal How Shane and Ilya’s First Meeting Was Actually Supposed to Happen
summary: The pivotal first scene of “Heated Rivalry,” in which hockey stars Shane and Ilya meet for the very first time, was written and filmed to be way longer than what viewers saw in the final cut.
story: It is a truth universally acknowledged that a good story starts with a good first line. In TODAY’s “Cold Open,” authors tease their buzzy upcoming release by revealing and explaining its first line, paragraph or page.

The pivotal first scene of the TV adaptation of “Heated Rivalry,” in which hockey stars Shane and Ilya meet for the very first time, was written and filmed to be way longer than what viewers saw in the final cut.

TODAY.com has an exclusive first look at “I’ll Believe in Anything,” a book about the making of Season 1 of “Heated Rivalry,” featuring scripts annotated by the show’s creator, writer and director, Jacob Tierney.

In an excerpt of the script, Tierney reveals that the first scene of the show — about a minute long in the episode’s final cut — was originally written to be up to six minutes. It sees a teenage Shane Hollander, played by Hudson Williams, introduce himself to another junior hockey prodigy, Ilya Rozanov, played by Connor Storrie, at a junior hockey tournament in Regina, Saskatchewan.
Fans of the show know that their meeting sets in motion a yearslong secret romantic tryst, occurring in the background of their respective rises through the ranks of professional hockey.

The scene starts with Shane awkwardly approaching Ilya outside a rink while the latter smokes a cigarette. In the final cut of Episode 1, they only exchange a few words. The two shake hands, Shane comments on the “no smoking” sign above Ilya’s head before calling the Russian “an awesome player to watch.” The teens taunt each other briefly before Shane heads inside.
But the annotated script reveals that their first conversation was much more substantial, with plenty of teasing.

“This was shot exactly as scripted, and then we cut it down,” Tierney writes. “Our editor Arthur Tarnowski would present an option of what a scene looks like at a minute and a half, or three minutes, six minutes, or whatever it was.”
The cut dialogue begins with Shane asking Ilya if his parents are at the tournament. After he answers no, Shane says, “That must suck. With Christmas and all.”
“Christmas is later in Russia,” Ilya says.
Awkward silence continues to ensure, and Shane finally breaks it by commenting on how next year’s event will occur in his hometown of Ottawa, Canada.
“Is Ottawa more exciting?” Ilya responds, after the stage directions note he “can’t help but smirk a bit at Shane’s nerves.”
After “they both kind of smile at each other,” Ilya makes the next remark, asking if Shane’s parents are with him.
“Yeah, they try to come to most of my games,” Shane says.
“Nice for you,” Ilya responds.
Tierney also describes his goal for how he wanted Shane and Ilya to come across to viewers in this first scene. He writes he wanted to show a “charming formality to Shane.”
“He’s trying to be a good sport and wants to introduce himself, and he has a bit of awkward-dad energy,” Tierney writes in the annotations.
Of Ilya, he adds, “I wanted people to watch Ilya go from suspicious to quite playful, to show that playfulness would come. It would be a hallmark of his personality.”
Read the full annotated scripts below.

title: Our 1 Question for Magnus Ferrell At Commercial: Where Did Will Ferrell’s Son Get His ‘Funky White Boy’ Sound?
summary: Magnus Ferrell talks about his dad, Will Ferrell, the success of his song “Asleep Talking” and what’s next.
story: When the camera cuts, the interview isn’t over. With “Cut for Time,” TODAY.com asks the burning questions our anchors couldn’t get to on air.
Magnus Ferrell is having a breakout moment, with a little help from his enthusiastic dad, Will Ferrell.
Earlier this year, Will Ferrell played a snippet of Magnus Ferrell’s song “Asleep Talking” during an appearance on Michelle Obama and her brother Craig Robinson’s podcast.
Their instantly genuine reactions led to a viral moment and a spotlight on the 22-year-old’s music, which he’s been making for years.

Magnus Ferrell, a sensitive, soulful crooner known for his falsetto voice and funky beat, may seem like a contrast to his father, whose voice has been famously likened to a “combination of Fergie and Jesus.”
But jazz musicianship is actually all in the family. Will Ferrell’s father, Roy Lee Ferrell, toured with the Righteous Brothers for 20 years.
We caught up with Magnus Ferrell after his appearance on TODAY with Jenna & Sheinelle on Sept. 30, where he also performed his breakout hit.

I had known known beforehand that was happening. I just knew that he was going to play the song. I was in Oregon at the time, and I had forgot that it was happening because the podcast interview (was taped) three or four weeks before. I’m in the middle of the woods with no cell service, and the only connection to the internet was the Wi-Fi in the cabin. I just kept running back and forth to the cabin into the woods, trying to be present where I was, but also trying to check in on this moment and my life dreams happening before my eyes, which was unbelievable.

I was kind of jaded to it because I’ve like been so lucky to have that my whole life. It was kind of a moment of like, oh my gosh, people don’t know him as a dad. They know him as the actor, and and we’ve kept the family side of things super private. It was just cool for everyone to see that moment and how he is as my dad. It meant a lot to me because that was his pure reaction. I’m just so lucky to have that support.
Yeah. I just never thought ever that my music would connect with that many people, but here we are.

I’ve been playing piano since I was 5 years old, and music has just kind of been a part of our family for a very long time. My dad’s dad, my grandpa, was a touring musician and toured with the Righteous Brothers. He played keys, piano, organ and alto sax.

Exactly, that’s where the groove comes from. This whole experience has made me just reflect on the past. There’s so many emotions of like, “S---, am I ready for this? Is this what I want to do? Is this like what I want my existence to be?”

I just think everything happens for a reason. I’ve been putting on music for five years now, so it’s been a while. I’ve had a lot of time to develop, which I’m very, very very thankful for. I’m really lucky that I wasn’t thrust into the spotlight when I put out my first song. I’m very sensitive, and I care a lot about my music. And I think if that had happened when I was younger and more green, it might have discouraged me from continuing.
One of the best things I’ve learned is not everybody’s going to like your music, so you have to really focus on making music for yourself that you can listen to.

I believe with the position that I’m in, I have this obvious advantage just in terms of spotlight. I’m the son of an actor. That’s going to be something that is just there. So I really pride myself on my work ethic and practicing my instruments, my vocals and my piano and all the other things I want to really get good at. I still think that there’s there’s a lot that I want to get better at, and I have a lot of potential to continue to improve. I’m not exactly where I want to be yet in terms of like my musicianship. I now feel really comfortable in the position I’m in. But yeah, I’m just excited to to just get better.

I grew up in jazz band and met one of my best friends and closest collaborators through jazz band. In terms of writing and putting out music together, that is something that I felt like was missing from the earlier music I was making. “Asleep Talking” was the first one that was like, “Oh, finally, this is what I’ve been searching for.” This is something that I would listen to on my own. I’m happy with how this sounds, and I’m not analyzing too much what’s going on. It’s not crafted too heavy.

I felt this way after an event and a certain experience that happened. We wrote about it. We tried to take the feeling of that event and put it into the song, and every part of it, I’m happy with. There’s not a thing that I’m like, “Oh, I wish we could have changed that. Oh, I wish this melody was different.” All of it, I’m happy with and satisfied.

It’s a really high honor, and I still got a lot to prove, you know. Just that world of like the funky white boy, like Justin Timberlake. It’s a lot to live up to, but I’m excited to do so and to take it as a challenge and an opportunity to show the world what my sound is and and just continue to make music that I love.
It was funny for sure. For the most part, I don’t get surprised by his antics, but that one caught me off guard.
The photo of me being looking like I’m mad is just the reaction, “Oh my god, you got me. I had no idea you were going to do this.” Normally I’m prepared but it completely caught me off guard

title: I’m a John Steinbeck Expert. This Is What I Really Think of Netflix’s ‘East of Eden’
summary: Two John Steinbeck experts unpack East of Eden and explain why they like the depiction of Cathy.
story: “Take it From Me” is a TODAY series where experts use their wisdom to explain trends or make recommendations within their fields.
Jeffrey Yeager sat down to watch the Netflix adaptation of the book he’s spent his career studying.

The vice president of the International Society of Steinbeck Scholars went into “East of Eden,” the seven-episode series directed and written by Zoë Kazan, with a “skeptical eye.” The show premiered just one day earlier, but he’d already heard chatter about how “it’s different than the book.”
Seven episodes later, he was won over by Kazan’s interpretation, which came over 60 years after her grandfather Elia Kazan directed the 1955 film adaptation.
“I came out very pleased. I thought it was fantastic,” Yeager tells TODAY.com.

“East of Eden” was the book Steinbeck considered his epic. At over 600 pages, the book is long enough to contain the origin stories of two sets of brothers, both loosely based on the Genesis story of Cain and Abel. The sprawling book, spanning the Civil War era to World War I, also maps out how two families came to live in California’s Salinas Valley: the Hamiltons and the Trasks.
Both the book and its characters are concerned with good and evil, free will and fate.
“Do our genes dictate who we are? Do our genes dictate the path we have in life, or do we have freedom in who we become?” Yeager summarizes the questions “East of Eden” asks.

Cal Trask (Joseph Zada in the show) is particularly consumed by these questions the more he finds out about his mother, Cathy Ames (Florence Pugh), and wonders if he’s destined to carry her less-than-golden legacy.
Steinbeck experts say Cathy’s nuanced depiction in Kazan’s “East of Eden” is what makes it so remarkable.

“I like the opening episode, and I like the fact that (Kazan) sets out the themes really clearly in terms of Cathy and the meditation on good and evil,” Susan Shillinglaw, a professor of English at San Jose State University who served as the university’s director of the Steinbeck Center for 18 years, tells TODAY.com.

In “East of Eden,” Steinbeck likens Cathy to a monster, writing in his introduction of the character, “The face and body may be perfect, but if a twisted gene or a malformed egg can produce physical monsters, may not the same process produce a malformed soul?”
According to Yeager, Cathy, in the book, is depicted as the “epitome of evil,” and “somebody who’s just missing something that is key to being human.”
Certainly, Cathy does evil things in both the TV show and book, including killing her own parents and attempting to kill the father of her twins (and that’s not all).
But Kazan says she set out to understand where Cathy’s monstrousness came from, reframing her childhood to include sexual assault.

Take the situation with her teacher as another example of how the show casts a different light on Cathy. In the book, she clearly manipulates a teacher to the point that he takes his own life. “But in the show, the teacher is trying to abuse her, and then she takes advantage of the situation,” Yeager says.
Rather than being wicked, Yeager says Pugh’s Cathy is “trying to redefine morality in her own way.”
Yeager applaudes Pugh’s performance, which shuffles between “reptilian eyes” and scenes that can draw empathy.

“I feel like the show can’t make its mind up on where it wants to go (with Cathy), and in some ways, that makes the show richer than the novel. It makes us think more about that character. How does evil come into the world?” Yeager says.
“The whole point of ‘East of Eden’ is to engage readers in an assessment of who Cathy is.”
For Shillinglaw, the show’s changing interpretations of Cathy are right in line with the legacy of the book.

“The whole point of ‘East of Eden’ is to engage readers in an assessment of who Cathy is,” Shillinglaw says. “She’s like the white whale in ‘Moby Dick.’ You have to keep looking at her. What does she mean? What is her purpose in the book?”
Yeager, after watching all seven episodes, wishes more attention had been given to the Hamiltons, the family Steinbeck based on his own.
“The Hamilton family was Steinbeck sort of tracing his lineage, and I can see why that wouldn’t be important for the story the show was trying to tell,” Yeager says.

He praises Hoon Lee’s “emotionally charged performance” as Lee, Aron and Cal Trask’s caretaker who plays an important role in healing the family at the end of the show. He’s also the voice of the story’s most overarching lesson: Timshel, a Hebrew word that’s translated to allow for free will in the triumph over evil, rather than fate.

For Shillinglaw, who taught a course on Steinbeck, says the conversations around “East of Eden” were always her favorite, and anticipates more brought on by the show, currently No. 1 on Netflix in the U.S.
“Students just found (the book) fascinating, and it was because of Cathy — what she meant and her legacy.”

title: ‘Days of Our Lives’ Star Robert Kelker-Kelly Dies at 62
summary: Longtime soap star Robert Kelker-Kelly, best known for portraying Bo Brady on “Days of Our Lives,” has died at age 62.
story: Longtime soap star Robert Kelker-Kelly, best known for portraying Bo Brady on “Days of Our Lives,” has died at age 62.
Kelly died on Oct. 3 in Missouri, according to a statement to NBC News by Kathleen Diebold Hargrave, the division director of the Office of the Regional Medical Examiner in St. Charles, Mo.
The cause of death is not available at this time, according to the statement. The timeline for death certification is normally 12 weeks, per the medical examiner’s office.
TMZ was first to report the news.
The Witchita, Kansas, native launched his daytime television career when he originated the role of Sam Fowler on “Another World” from 1987 until 1990.
He began playing rebel-turned-police detective Bo Brady on “Days of Our Lives” in 1992 after Peter Reckell, the actor who originated the role nearly a decade before, left the series.
Kelker-Kelly’s character was embroiled in a love triangle alongside Hope Brady, played by Kristian Alfonso, and Billie Reed, played by Lisa Rinna.

Rinna made headlines earlier this year when she detailed her challenging behind-the-scenes relationship with Kelker-Kelly in her memoir, “You Better Believe I’m Gonna Talk About It: A Candid New York Times Bestselling Memoir of Hollywood, Aging, and Owning It All.”
Kelker-Kelly left “Days of Our Lives” when Reckell resumed the role of Bo in 1995.
Kelker-Kelly returned to “Another World” from 1996 to 1998 to play professional race car driver Bobby Reno, who was later revealed to be Dr. Shane Roberts.
The actor next took on the role of Stavros Cassadine on “General Hospital,” appearing in more than 40 episodes from 2001 to 2014.
Kelker-Kelly won a Soap Opera Digest Award in 1994 for outstanding lead actor and another the following year for hottest soap couple, which he shared with Rinna.
Kelker-Kelly was married to fellow “Days of our Lives” star Miriam Parrish from 1997 until 2013, according to IMDB.

title: Anna Camp Is Nearly Unrecognizable on TODAY After Dramatic Hair Transformation
summary: Anna Camp traded in her blond hair for brown hair and showed off the new look in a TODAy appearance on October 6.
story: The blonde look that was Anna Camp’s signature in everything from “True Blood” to “Pitch Perfect” over more than 15 years has given way to her “brunette era.”

The actor had some fans doing a double take when she first revealed her new hair on Instagram in September. She also showed off the brunette look on TODAY Oct. 6 to promote her new HGTV show, “A Very Haunted Renovation.”
“The same but different.. brunette era loading now 🧉” Camp wrote on Instagram Sept. 7.
Fans were on board with the dramatic change from the blonde look she has worn as a vampire, snobby sorority sister, “Scream 7” horror queen and blonde twins on “You.”
“Beautiful! I mean you look good either way, blonde or brunette. 🤎” one fan commented.
“I mean… gorgeous either way! ❤️” another wrote.
“Looks great!” another commented.
One fan asked Camp what color her natural hair is.
“A little lighter than this!” she replied.
Camp, 44, still has the platinum blonde look on her new HGTV show, which features a renovation competition at one of America’s most haunted homes.
In keeping with the haunted theme, the actor will also be returning to the stage in a production of “2:22 A Ghost Story” at the Lucille Lortel Theatre in New York City in October.
“I like the spooky stuff and Halloween’s coming up, so it’s my season, I’m excited,” she said on TODAY.

title: Jenna Bush Hager Says Her October 2026 Book Club Pick Is By an Author on Her ‘Mt. Rushmore of Writers’
summary: The October Read With Jenna book club pick for October 2026 is Partita by Barbara Kingsolver.
story: Jenna Bush Hager picked a book by one of her “all-time favorite” authors for her October book club selection: “Partita” by Barbara Kingsolver.
“She’s on the Mt. Rushmore of writers for me,” Jenna says.
“Partita” is a followup to Kingsolver’s massive hit “Demon Copperhead,” which won the Pulitzer Prize in 2023.
It’s about a woman named Livia who looks back at her first romance when he unexpectedly contacts her decades after they met when she was studying piano in college.
“When a great love from her past comes back into her future, it has her ask the question, ‘How has my life ended up? Has it centered around the things I thought it would?” Jenna asks.
She says she loves the book because of how intimate it is. “It centers around what makes life beautiful,” she says.

The title, “Partita,” is a reference to a type of musical composition that is literally in parts. The theme is reflected in how the book weaves together the many parts of Livia’s life, as well as the events that shatter her life into those parts.
“We know within the first page Livia loses her brother, which sets her off on a journey to put the broken pieces of her together,” she says.
Jenna points to the epilogue of the book, which is a quote by Toni Morrison: “Sometimes you don’t survive whole. You just survive in part. But the grandeur in life is that attempt.”
"Partita" by Barbara Kingsolver

Kingsolver has been publishing books since 1988. Her 1999 book “The Poisonwood Bible” was a Pulitzer finalist, and she won the prize in 2023 for “Demon Copperhead.” Both novels were selected for Oprah’s Book Club.

title: Inspired by ‘90s Nostalgia and ‘Scooby-Doo’, The Lawrence Brothers Launch New Graphic Novel
summary: During a family vacation, the Lawrence brothers joked about starting a detective agency.
story: During a family vacation, the Lawrence brothers joked about starting a detective agency.

A guest at where they were vacationing had misplaced a valuable piece of jewelry while at the beach, Joey Lawrence tells TODAY.com. As the investigation continued, he, along with brothers Matt and Andrew Lawrence, began creating fictional storylines about finding the “lost treasure.” In one scenario, Matt even got a bad sunburn, before shedding his skin to reveal that he was the villain of the story. The ideas kept coming.

So after years of “fooling around with the idea,” the trio finally decided to team up with the Berkowitz Brothers, Ben and Max Berkowitz, Sean Von Gorman and Z2 to bring “The Lawrence Brothers Detective Agency,” an original graphic novel series, to life.

“The Lawrence Brothers Detective Agency” can best be described as a series about “three brothers whose knack for getting into trouble is only matched by their talent for solving mysteries,” Andy tells TODAY.com. “Every case brings clues, chaos, nostalgia, and the kind of brotherly love that only us Lawrence brothers can deliver.”
The siblings have a long history of collaborating on screen, starting with their 1995 sitcom “Brotherly Love,” along with “Horse Sense,” “Jumping Ship,” “Mistletoe Mixup” and more.
A graphic novel, on the other hand, is something new and creative for the trio.

“We’ve been throwing around this idea for years. We wanted to do sort of a grown up ‘Scooby-Doo’ meets ‘Hardy Boys’ and it just kind of came together,” Joey says. “We threw in some ‘90s nostalgia because it’s all the craze.”
Inspired by the Scooby Gang, in the first graphic novel they included nods to the franchise by including a mystery van and other “hidden Mickeys” that would make millennials nostalgic.
The first installment, out now, is the detective agency’s origin story.
“We love the fact that you can really take a lot of chances in this type of format, and that’s what we always loved about comic books and animated series,” Matt says.
Because they “know each other so well,” Andy says, their decadeslong working relationship just flows. Matt adds that when it comes to getting creative, they all come at it from very different angles.
“The sum of the three parts is always going to be better than us individually, in my opinion,” he says.
Calling this graphic novel among their most “unique” projects together, they first hoped to create an animated series.
“An adult ‘Scooby-Doo,’” Joey says, adding that they would “edge up the rating” for an older audience. “I feel like you could have so much fun with that.”
They aim to expand the universe with additional cases and, yes, one day create an animated series or perhaps a live-action show.
For now, Matt says, “Every novel that we put out would be a different case that we would take on. So at the end of this one, not to give too much away, we kind of say: We’re open for business.”

title: How ‘Sister Wives’ Stars Reacted to Kody Brown Not Being on the Show for the 1st Time in 16 Years
summary: Why is Kody Brown not on Sister Wives? How Christine, Janelle and Meri reacted to him not being on the show.
story: “Sister Wives” returned for Season 21 on Oct. 4 without its longtime star, Kody Brown.
For 16 years, the TLC series has followed as Kody and his four wives and their children navigated life in a plural marriage.

Brown and his only remaining wife, Robyn, left the series before filming for the new season began, forcing Kody Brown’s ex-wives  — Janelle, Christine and Meri —  to react to the couple’s exit on camera.

“I don’t know how to process it all. I’m just going to be honest. No idea how I feel about this whole thing,” Christine said in a confessional, adding, “ It’s just bizarre they’re done ... I don’t know what it means. I have no idea.”
In her own confessional, Janelle revealed she was “very shocked” to hear Kody and Robin would not be returning to the show.
Kody and Robin’s abrupt exit comes after years of upheaval in the family.
In 2021, Christine ended her spiritual marriage to Kody after 25 years and six children together.
Not long after, Janelle ended her union with Kody after nearly 30 years and six children.
Janelle and Kody also shared in the tragic loss of their son Garrison, who died in 2024.

Both Christine and Janelle went on to find love with new partners: In 2023, Christine tied the knot with David Woolley, and Janelle went public in August with a new boyfriend named Pete, who appears on “Sister Wives” this season.
Kody and Robin, who was originally his fourth wife, legally married in 2014 after Kody legally divorced Meri.
Already a mom of three, Robin went on to welcome two children, Solomon and Ariella, with Kody.
With feelings bitter among Kody and his exes by the end of Season 20, Kody vowed to do a “pilgrimage” to “apologize” to all three of the women.
The Season 21 premiere included footage from those apologies, which Janelle said Kody did to boost his image.

“I feel like the apology tour was, in the end, something he was trying to redeem himself with, and I don’t think it was necessarily that sincere because there’s been no contact since,” Janelle said in a confessional.

“He very publicly torpedoed my character afterwards, so I’m like, yeah, whatever,” Janelle added, addressing Kody’s public claim that Janelle tried to arrange deal with Kody to sell the family’s Coyote Pass property in Flagstaff, Arizona, behind Meri’s back.
“All of the sudden, here, months after the deal is closed, he starts talking about how I was doing this backdoor deal,” Janelle said. “I was like, ‘Where did that come from?’”
“I was not scheming. If I had been scheming, you would not have known it,” Janelle added.
Janelle described Kody’s public accusation as “a final f--- you” to her.
“It’d be one thing if he just said it, but everybody’s believing him,” said Janelle.
During the episode, Janelle asked Meri to meet with her in person so she could clear the air about what Kody said about the property deal.
“I’m frustrated that he wants to continue to stir up the drama. I don’t want to give him that kind of power,” Janelle told Meri.
“It got really way more complicated than it needed to be, and I don’t know why,” Janelle said, adding, “But, it’s done, and I was not trying to cut you out of a deal.”
The episode concluded by showing Janelle, Meri and Christine putting their tensions aside to reunite and sort through family photos together.
The news was confirmed in the Season 21 trailer in released in mid September, with a title card that said, “After 16 years of filming ‘Sister Wives,’ Kody & Robyn will not be returning to the show.”
TODAY.com has reached out to Kody and TLC for comment.

title: Aaron Sorkin Says Jeremy Strong Was in Character 24/7: ‘Never Heard Him Speak in His Own Voice’
summary: Jeremy Strong’s portrayal of Mark Zuckerberg in the new movie “The Social Reckoning” did not end when the cameras stopped filming for the day.
story: Jeremy Strong’s portrayal of Mark Zuckerberg in the new movie “The Social Reckoning” did not end when the cameras stopped filming for the day.
Director Aaron Sorkin shared on TODAY Oct. 5 how the Emmy-winning “Succession” star brought his famously immersive acting method to the role of the Facebook and Meta co-founder.

“Jeremy Strong who gives a thunderous performance in the film is, yes, he’s an immersive actor,” Sorkin told Craig Melvin. “He showed up on the first day, I never heard him speak in his own voice. He only spoke, moved, behaved as Mark Zuckerberg, not just on the set, but when he went home too, 24 hours a day.”

A 2021 profile of Strong in the New Yorker broke down how he fully inhabited the role of Kendall Roy in “Succession,” which he called “identity diffusion,” rather than Method acting. The story describes Strong dressing like Roy in his regular life and staying in character to the point of concern from castmate Brian Cox.
Strong, 47, brought that same dedication to his portrayal of Zuckerberg, one of the most well-known tech moguls in the world.

“I know it seems weird, I know it seems perhaps even unnecessary, but the results speak for themselves,” Sorkin said. “It’s not silly, it’s not nonsense, it’s not like he doesn’t know we’re making a movie. He sees the crew and the cameras. This is his process, and I don’t think he knows any other way to do it.”
The new film, which hits theaters on Oct. 9, is the sequel to Sorkin’s Oscar-winning 2010 film “The Social Network” about Zuckerberg and the controversial origin of Facebook.

The movie tells the story of a 2021 leak by former Facebook employee and whistleblower Frances Haugen, played by Oscar winner Mikey Madison. She told the U.S. Senate in a 2021 hearing that it’s “clear that Facebook prioritizes profit over the well-being of children and all users” and said the company is “accountable to no one.”
Zuckerberg responded publicly by sharing an internal memo to staff that the company’s work has been mischaracterized.
Sorkin called the sequel “a whistleblower story” in the vein of iconic journalism films like “All the President’s Men,” “The Insider” and “Spotlight.”

“The film shouldn’t be political, unless you’re somebody who’s anti the truth,” Sorkin said. “The film is saying that the truth is important, and we’re not getting it. So unless you’re anti the truth, you shouldn’t find the film political, but yes, it’s going to be seen as political, primarily because of the final climactic sequence.”

title: Does Olivia Dean’s New Song Sound Like Bill Withers’ 1981 Hit ‘Just the Two of Us’? A New Lawsuit Says So
summary: How similar does Olivia Dean’s “I’ve Seen It” sound like Bill Withers’ Just the Two of Us?” Listen to the two songs.
story: Olivia Dean is facing allegations that one of her songs rips off a classic hit by R&B legend Bill Withers.

A new lawsuit claims the London-born Grammy winner, 27, steals a melody from Withers’ 1981 hit “Just the Two of Us” on “I’ve Seen It,” the closing track on her breakout hit album “The Art of Loving,” NBC News correspondent Joe Fryer reported Oct. 5 on TODAY.

The lawsuit was filed by Mattie Music Group, the publisher of Withers’ music catalog, against Dean’s music labels and publisher. Dean and her cowriters on “I’ve Seen It,” Bastian Langebaek and Max Wolfgang, are not directly named as defendants.

The lawsuit claims similarities between certain melodies in “I’ve Seen It” and “Just the Two of Us,” which Withers cowrote with William Salter and Ralph MacDonald and recorded with saxophonist Grover Washington Jr., are “obvious and inescapable.”

The lawsuit specifically compares the melody around the lyrics “I’ve heard it laced in every song and still words all come out wrong” in Dean’s song with the melody around the lyrics “I see the crystal raindrops fall and the beauty of it all…” in Withers’ song.
The lawsuit alleges the two songs’ shared musical features are “so striking,” and “did not result from coincidence, independent creation, or reliance on common musical elements.”

Dean, who won the Best New Artist award at the 2026 Grammys and is best known for the current pop hits “Man I Need” and “It’s So Easy (To Fall in Love),” spoke about being inspired by classic R&B music during an October 2025 visit to TODAY.
“I love songwriting and I love Motown and soul music, Aretha Franklin, music that makes you feel something and tells a story. I think its timeless,” Dean said.
The new lawsuit reignites a tricky debate that’s raged for decades in the music world: Where is the line drawn between artistic inspiration and theft?

Music journalist Tomás Mier told Fryer there’s been an uptick in music copyright lawsuits in recent years. “These estates are being a lot more particular with the sound similarities and going and being a little bit more litigious,” Mier said.

In 2015, the family of R&B legend Marvin Gaye won a landmark copyright infringement lawsuit when they successfully sued singer Robin Thicke and Pharrell Williams, arguing their 2013 hit “Blurred Lines” infringed upon the copyright of Gaye’s 1977 hit “Got to Give It Up.”
A federal court, and later an appeals court, agreed that “Blurred Lines” copied Gaye’s hit and ordered Thicke and Williams to pay nearly $5 million to Gaye’s estate in the case’s final ruling.

More recently, British singer Ed Sheeran triumphed against the family of one of Gaye’s co-songwriters in a legal battle that alleged Sheeran’s 2014 hit “Thinking Out Loud” copied elements of Gaye’s 1973 hit “Let’s Get It On.”
In May 2023, a Manhattan federal jury unanimously ruled that Sheeran and his co-writer on “Thinking Out Loud,” Amy Wadge, did not steal from Gaye on their song.
While the case was ongoing, Sheeran criticized such lawsuits in a video shared on social media.
Sheeran explained in his video that “coincidences” in songwriting are “bound to happen.”
“Its really damaging to the song writing industry,” Sheeran said. “There’s only so many notes and very few chords used in pop music.

title: Hoda Kotb Wipes Away Tears in an Emotional Tribute to the Saints’ ‘Domecoming’ Game 20 Years Ago
summary: Hoda Kotb looks back on the 20th anniversary of the Domecoming game in an emotional segment.
story: It’s been 20 years since that magical night, but just recalling the emotions of the New Orleans’ Saints first game back at the Superdome after Hurricane Katrina was enough to leave Hoda Kotb and Drew Brees wiping away tears.

Hoda and the legendary Saints quarterback recalled on TODAY Oct. 5 how a battered city in desperate need of hope and joy was focused on the Saints when they took the field in September 2006 for their first home game back in the Superdome.

“We took so much strength from our fans,” Brees said. “Truly, that night was a symbolic moment where we, as New Orleanians, had the opportunity to show the rest of the world, not only are we coming back, but we’re coming back stronger than ever.”
Their showdown against the visiting Atlanta Falcons came just over a year after Hurricane Katrina had devastated New Orleans in August 2025, laying waste to large swaths of the city.

The Superdome, a site of so much joy on Sundays, became a place of despair and horror as a shelter of last resort for displaced residents in the wake of the storm. The Saints didn’t play any games there in the 2005 season because it took 10 months of repairs to fix the damage to the iconic stadium.
Fans were able to put aside their hardships for a night when New Orleans celebrated its “Domecoming” game with a rousing 23-3 win that marked a milestone in the rebirth of the city.

Hoda, a diehard Saints fan and former news anchor in New Orleans, caught up with Brees as New Orleans gets set to mark the 20th anniversary of that night. Members of the 2006 team will be in attendance when the Saints play the Falcons on ESPN’s Monday Night Football Oct. 5 to commemorate the game.

Brees, now 47, had chosen to sign with New Orleans as a free agent ahead of the 2006 season despite the devastation that the franchise had suffered. He had suffered a potentially career-ending shoulder injury a year earlier while on the then-San Diego Chargers, so he saw New Orleans as a situation where both sides needed each other.

“Brittany and I looked at each other and said, ‘This is God’s calling in our life. Like, we belong here,’” Brees said about his wife. “This is about so much greater than just football. And how many opportunities do you get in your life to be a part of something like that?”
Hoda and Brees both became emotional when she asked him why he decided to come to a situation that many free agents would not have even considered.

“I was in a really tough place in my career,” he continued. “I was in this place where I was yearning for somebody to believe in me. And New Orleans was here, wanting someone to believe in them. And that’s where the match happened.”
Hoda dabbed away tears while Brees also teared up.
“Look at us,” Brees said.

The Saints were coming off a 3-13 season, but with Brees and new head coach Sean Payton now in the fold, there was optimism that things could turn around in 2006. It would all start in the first game back in the Superdome.
Payton conducted the team’s final practice before the Falcons game in the stadium rather than the team’s practice facility.

“All of a sudden, the lights go out,” Brees said. “And then here’s footage from the storm and interviews with members of the community. Not a dry eye in the house. And Sean looks at us, and he goes, ‘I don’t need to tell you that Monday night is going to be special.’ He’s like, ‘But it’s only special if you win.’”
The team took the field to a deafening roar from the home crowd in a nationally televised game on ESPN.
“Quite simply, tonight is the most significant New Orleans Saints game ever,” announcer Mike Tirico said on the broadcast.
Tirico, who is now the play-by-play announcer for Sunday Night Football on NBC, recalled the energy of that night.
“For that team to come back and that city to have one of its central heartbeats back was a real powerful message, and you felt it when you walked in the building,” Tirico said on TODAY Oct. 5.

Less than two minutes into the game, a play occurred that has since been immortalized in a statue outside the stadium. Special teams dynamo Steve Gleason sprinted into the backfield and dove to block a punt by the Falcons. Teammate Curtis Deloatch pounced on the loose ball in the end zone for a touchdown to send the home crowd into pandemonium.

“Just the way that that erupted the whole building. You ask anybody, and it is the loudest they have ever heard the Dome,” Brees said. “It was that moment. It was, like, there is nobody that would beat us tonight.”
Gleason, 49, has since become an inspirational figure for his fight against amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) in retirement.
When Deloatch recovered the blocked punt for a score, Tirico kept it simple for a reason when he shouted, “Touchdown, New Orleans!”

“In the lead up to that week, in my mind, I said, ‘Well, if the Saints score, I want to make sure that I say, ‘Touchdown, New Orleans,’ because that was the night that it wasn’t about the Saints — it was about the city,” Tirico said.
Gleason’s heroics kicked off a cathartic night for fans in desperate need of one.

“I remember that night seeing faces in those sections that were around the booth, and the tears were real,” Tirico said. “The smiles, the cheers, were profound, joyous, natural, never-ending. And that’s why, 20 years later, that night stays with me.”

That game also kickstarted a rejuvenation of the Saints franchise that culminated in New Orleans winning its first and only Super Bowl during the 2009 season. Brees, who retired in 2021, went on to become a Pro Football Hall of Famer synonymous with the city.
“You have a bond,” he said about his relationship with the fans.
He and many of his former teammates will be in the Superdome on Oct. 5 when the Saints (1-2) take on the Falcons (1-2) on an emotional night.
“When you do incredible things like that with people and do hard things like that with people, you’re connected for life,” Brees said.
Brees is looking forward to once again hearing the voices of New Orleans fans that have echoed for 20 years.
“For the reopening of the Dome, it’s going to feel like it was yesterday,” he said. “And I’m sure that crowd is going to be a little wild, too, so we’re going to get ‘em riled up.”

title: Mabel Lowe, Daughter of Chad Lowe, Pays Tribute To Late 13-Year-Old Sister Fiona
summary: Mabel Lowe — daughter of actor Chad Lowe and his wife, producer Kim Painter — recently shared some sweet words in remembrance of her 13-year-old sister Fiona, who died Sept. 29.
story: Mabel Lowe — daughter of actor Chad Lowe and his wife, producer Kim Painter — recently shared some sweet words in remembrance of her 13-year-old sister Fiona, who died Sept. 29.
Mabel Lowe, 17, posted a tribute on Instagram Oct. 3, promising to honor her sister’s legacy. According to the County of Los Angeles Medical Examiner, Fiona Lowe’s death was ruled a suicide.

“I love you so much fiona ❤️ i wish your short time here was easier and i hope your mind is at ease now,” Mabel Lowe wrote in the post. “I will honor you forever and keep your memory alive. I love you, i hope you knew just how much.”
The sisters, in addition to Nixie, 10, are the children of Chad Lowe and Painter.
In her post, Mabel Lowe shared several photos, ranging from snaps of Fiona as a toddler through her preteen years, along with a video of the two dancing together in Halloween outfits.
The emotional tribute follows a Sept. 30 statement from the family that was shared on Mabel Lowe’s Instagram story.
“We are deeply heartbroken by the loss of our beloved Fiona,” the family wrote in the statement. “She was a loving young girl who was smart, creative and loved to dance.
The statement also said that Fiona was “adored by her sisters and she was deeply loved by her parents.”
“In fact, she was the light of our lives,” the statement said. “Her passing is devastating for our entire family and we ask for prayers and privacy at this time.”
The family did not mention a cause of death at the time, but encouraged those with mental health struggles to seek help.
“If you or someone you know is struggling with mental health, please reach out to the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline by calling or texting 988,” they wrote.
Months ago, Chad Lowe, the younger brother of fellow actor Rob Lowe, had shared a post in celebration of Fiona’s 13th birthday.
“Celebrating Fiona officially becoming a teen today!!” he wrote in November 2025. “Keep dancing through life FiBear! Love you soooo much!!❤️❤️❤️❤️❤️❤️❤️❤️❤️❤️❤️❤️❤️”

According to data from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, suicide is the second-leading cause of death among youth ages 10-14 in the U.S. Further, one-fifth of high-schoolers report serious thoughts about suicide while 9% report a suicide attempt.
Nonprofit National Alliance on Mental Illness encourages individuals who are concerned for loved ones to “seek help and support before the crisis emerges.”

“If you or someone you love begins to feel worried but doesn’t feel in immediate danger of acting on thoughts of self-harm or suicide, then steps should be taken to find help for care and support,” the organization wrote on its website. “This help can be from a pediatrician, primary health care provider, or a mental health clinician.”

title: Ciara And Her Baby Bump Tear Up Paris Fashion Week Catwalk
summary: Ciara, who’s pregnant with her fifth child, strutted the catwalk for avante-garde designer Junya Watanabe on Oct. 3 during the highly-anticipated week of looks in the City of Love.
story: Ciara has leveled up the runway at Paris Fashion Week.
The singer, who’s pregnant with her fifth child, strutted the catwalk for avante-garde designer Junya Watanabe on Oct. 3 during the highly-anticipated week of looks in the City of Love.
Her walk made extra special as she was accompanied by her baby bump.
The walk marked  an emotional moment for the artist herself. She wrote in an Instagram post shortly after the event that she “held back tears while experiencing THIS MOMENT.”

“I’ve always dreamed of walking the runway in Paris. @JunyaWatanabe having me walk in your show was a Major Dream Come True!” Ciara wrote in the Oct. 3 post. “I was honestly afraid that when I mentioned I was with child, you say it doesn’t fit the vision anymore, but you said YES!!”

Ciara rocked three different looks for the Junya Watanabe Spring/Summer 2027 show. One featured a trench coat over a matching crop top and leggings set, paired with hot red pointed-toe shoes. It was tied together with a cap adorned with metal chains.
For another look, Ciara wore a long headpiece that resembled a hanging chandelier.
The singer also wore a shredded leather motorcycle jacket, held together by zippers and long strands of pearls.

The eye-catching outfits didn’t stop there for the singer. After the show, she attended a gala held by fashion and digital media company the Business of Fashion. For the occasion, she rocked a stunning sheer black dress, accented by black floral appliqués.

The singer announced the news of her pregnancy in a Sept. 6 video shared on Instagram. This will be her fourth child with husband and former NFL player Russell Wilson. She has a 12-year-old son with ex-fiancé rapper Future.

title: Link From ‘Zelda’ and Jason From ‘GTA6’ Face Off on ‘SNL’ In Chaotic Weekend Update
summary: The Weekend Update segment of the latest episode of “Saturday Night Live” dove right into the hype surrounding the upcoming November release of “Grand Theft Auto VI.”
story: Oh, it’s on.
The Weekend Update segment of the latest episode of “Saturday Night Live” dove right into the hype surrounding the upcoming November release of “Grand Theft Auto VI.”
As co-host Colin Jost pointed out, most video games moved their release dates to avoid competition with the long-awaited game — that is, except for “Legend of Zelda: The Ocarina of Time.”

In true “SNL” fashion, the Update desk invited the star characters of both games — Link from “Zelda,” played by Mikey Day in some pretty ridiculous cosplay, and Jason from “GTA6,” played by Marcello Hernandez — to duke it out. And it didn’t take long for absolute chaos to unfold.

“Respect to all the Zelda games, they’re all right, but they’re all TMPNG: Too Many Puzzles, No Guns,” Jason says at one point during the showdown, before pulling out a toy rocket-propelled grenade. “Look at what you can buy at a store in ‘GTA 6.’ You can just buy this, man! You can just buy it like it’s Advil at a store!”
Link attempts to counter Jason’s attack.
“You want to talk badass? How about this fairy in a box?” Link yells back. “You can just buy this! Three magic frogs and it gets you this!”
You gotta admit. Link’s got a point there.

“GTA 6” is slated to revolve around Jason and his partner Lucia as they take on the fictional Vice City in a Bonnie-and-Clyde style dynamic. “Legend of Zelda: The Ocarina of Time,” is a remake of a 1998 game in which Link works to defeat the villainous monster Ganondorf.
The two, who battle it out in front of Jost and Weekend Update co-host Michael Che, begin with a pretty fierce argument about Link’s outfit.

“The only way this is like ‘Barbenheimer’ is that I blow stuff up and he looks like a little blonde girl,” Jason says in response to Jost’s comparison to the double feature “Barbie” and “Oppenheimer” which premiered on the same day in July 2023.
Link immediately disagrees with Jason, who hits back with, “What do you mean? You got like a little green dress on.”
“Shows what you know,” Link says defensively. “This is my adventure tunic. God, you’re such an idiot.”
They also compare lifestyles. While Jason brags about stealing vehicles, robbing banks and womanizing, Link shows off his ...very different routine.
“Meanwhile, over in Hyrule, I woke up, bought magic beans from a shopkeeper, then played my ocarina,” Link says.
By the end of their debate, we’d say that the games sound pretty even.
The sixth installment of the “Grand Theft Auto” franchise comes over 10 years after its previous game. It arrives on Nov. 19, roughly two weeks after “Zelda’s” release on Nov. 5.

title: Lizzo Dedicates Kids Book to Late Father Who ‘Overly Embraced’ Her Passion For The Flute
summary: Before artist Lizzo went on to win four Grammys and sell out major stadiums, she had role models who were encouraging her to dream big, she told Sunday Sitdown.
story: Before artist Lizzo went on to win four Grammys and sell out major stadiums, she had role models who were encouraging her to dream big.

During her chat with host Willie Geist on TODAY’s Oct. 4 Sunday Sitdown, Lizzo, who’s currently promoting her new book “Lil Lizzo Meets Sasha B. Flootin,’” reflected on the elements of her upbringing that led to her success. Her late father Michael Jefferson, to whom the book is dedicated, is one standout influence, she said.

“When I started playing the flute, I was so nervous that it would not be accepted by my family ‘cause my family’s so cool, you know?And I took the nerdy route,” Lizzo, 38, explained to Willie. “My dad actually overly embraced my flute-playing. And he actually saw bigger dreams for me than I saw for myself.”
The new book follows character Lil Lizzo’s adventures from her band room to places like the sea and outer space, as she discovers her love for the flute.
The artist told Willie that Lil Lizzo’s love for the instrument draws from her own passion —one that was fostered by her father, who passed away in 2009.
Lizzo shared how her father used to call on her to perform “The Carnival of Venice,” a classic song made famous by composer Niccolò Paganini, for his friends.
“I would play it, and he’d be like, ‘Look how talented she is,’” Lizzo recalled to Willie. “‘She’s gonna play in big stadiums one day.’”
Lizzo, who performed that very song at New York City jazz club The Blue Note in March, said that it was important for her to pay tribute to her biggest fan.
“I dedicated this (book) to him because I wanted him to know that he was right,” she added.

During her chat with Willie, she also gave a shoutout to another notable figure from her childhood — her fifth grade band director and teacher. She said he infused hip hop and R&B into her lessons even before she adopted the blended-genre as her signature sound.

“He would write down all the big songs of the day and he would transcribe it and put it into sheet music for us,” Lizzo explained. “So, instead of having traditional ‘Hot Cross Buns’ or whatever, we would have this handwritten sheet music that he would Xerox and put on our music stands.”
She ended up taking the style with her, Lizzo said.

“Even when I was in high school, I would be writing all of the big rap songs that came out for our marching band so that we could play it at the football games and actually be a cool band, ‘cause we were always playin‘ the nerdy stuff,” she said.
For her book, Lizzo said she also drew inspiration from her own journey as an artist.

“I think you have to make a choice as an author, like, what kind of book you wanna create,” said Lizzo, who later crowned herself the “Eminem of children’s book authors.” “I think I am a rapper. So I wanted it to feel like rap. If you played a beat, you could read Sasha B. Flootin’ and Lil Lizzo to a beat, and it would be a song.”
And so, her writing in the story mirrored elements of her songs, she said.

“I know that kids, we love iambic pentameter. So that was really important to me as I was writing the story,” she told Willie. “I knew what the story was gonna be, but I’m like, ‘How do I bring it to life?’”
Willie praised the artist for being “able to rhyme ‘jam’ with ‘ham,’ and not the food, ham, a different kind.”
“Thank you for seeing me,” Lizzo said.

title: Watch Taylor Swift Crash Dakota Johnson’s ‘SNL’ Monologue Like A True Friend
summary: Actor Dakota Johnson got a little visit from her therapist, er, BFF while hosting the Oct. 3 episode of “Saturday Night Live.”
story: Actor Dakota Johnson got a little visit from her therapist, er, BFF while hosting the Oct. 3 episode of “Saturday Night Live.”

The “Verity” actor delivered a monologue for the sketch comedy show in which she referenced the good friends in her life who never judge her for her dating choices. Of course, one of these said good friends crashed the stage — none other than pop icon Taylor Swift.
Johnson introduced her pal as her “literal therapist” who she leans on amid a rocky dating life. And things went off the rails.
“I’m not your therapist actually,” Swift said after joining Johnson on the Studio 8H stage. “Actually, you just show up once a week at my house with an empty bottle of wine and ask if I want some.”
Johnson defended herself.
“Yeah, I have manners,” she said.
But Swift wasn’t done.
“Then you flop on my couch and overshare, and every so often I just say, ‘Damn, that’s crazy,’” the recording artist said.
Johnson, who’s hosted the show twice before, kicked off the second episode of the new season of “SNL.” She was accompanied by musical guest Baltimore hardcore band Turnstile.
Swift popped in a second time during her friend’s big night to bring out a cake for Johnson, who turned 37 at the stroke of midnight.

Johnson has also appeared in Swift’s projects. Most recently, she starred Swift’s music video for “Patient Zero,” which premiered at the MTV Video Music Awards Sept. 27. In it, Johnson and Swift appear to bond over a toxic ex, played by Colin Farrell, before a twist ending reveals the shocking reality.
“Giggling with your friend because you’re twinning for an entire shoot was a new and truly delightful experience,” Swift wrote in an Instagram post about making the video with Johnson.

title: Watch Anne Hathaway ‘Disappear’ After Promoting A Marathon Of 5 Movies This Year
summary: After a year of promoting a whopping five major films, Anne Hathaway made good on her promise to get out of the spotlight.
story: After a year of promoting a whopping five major films, Anne Hathaway made good on her promise to get out of the spotlight.

The actor shared a video on her Instagram Oct. 2 —the release day of her latest film “Verity” — in which she hilariously disappears into thin air. It comes after the actor told Entertainment Tonight in a Sept. 21 clip that she had been planning to “to vanish in a plume of smoke” after her press tours were over.
Hathaway, who’s also pregnant with her third child, sure has a sense of humor.
In the clip, Hathaway speaks to the camera, telling fans that she’s “heading out to the ‘Verity’ premiere.”
“‘Verity’ comes out in theaters Friday, Oct. 2, and then on Oct. 3...,” Hathaway says before abruptly vanishing from the screen as a puff of animated smoke dissipates in the room.
The video then features a flurry of faux news stories.
“Anne Hathaway simply evaporates,” one headline says.
The clip concludes with some words from the actor, thanking her fans.
“Thank you everyone for your support, and for making this an incredible, unforgettable year,” the text says.
Now that’s how you end a press circuit.
The hilarious post comes after Hathaway not only promoted “Verity,” but also did press for “The Devil Wears Prada 2,” “Mother Mary,” “The Odyssey” and “The End of Oak Street.”
Her ubiquity in film this year led satirical outlet The Onion to release a now-viral article in August titled, “Analysts Warn U.S. Economy Becoming Overly Dependent On Anne Hathaway.”
In addition to the nonstop press tours, Hathaway is also pregnant, expecting her third child with husband Adam Schulman. The two share sons Jonathan, 10, and Jack, 6.
The actor said during her Sept. 30 appearance on “The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon,” that she got the news that she was expecting just before she was set to promote one of her films.

“I found out I was pregnant like, two-and-a-half weeks before ‘The Devil Wears Prada 2’ press tour kicked off,” said Hathaway, who announced her pregnancy in June. “And I was just like, ‘How is that gonna work?’”
While it’s been quite the amount of work, Hathaway told the Associated Press that it’s not necessary to “over praise the pampered actress.”

“There’s a lot of pregnant women out there at home and in the workplace who didn’t get a manicure this morning,” she told the outlet in a Sept. 29 interview. “I’m very happy to do my job. I have so much support.”

title: Dennis Miller’s Fellow ‘Monday Night Football’ Announcer Fondly Recalls the ‘Experiment’ to Add Him to the Booth
summary: Dan Fouts recalls being on “Monday Night Football” with Dennis Miller for their two-season run on the broadcast.
story: It was an audacious move.

In an effort to jumpstart interest in “Monday Night Football,” ABC hired Dennis Miller to serve as part of the broadcast team in the booth in 2000, joining play-by-play legend Al Michaels and Pro Football Hall of Famer Dan Fouts, who served as color analyst.

It was a move met with cheers and jeers at the time. Don Ohlmeyer, who had produced “MNF” during its glory days with Howard Cosell, Frank Gifford and Don Meredith, returned to the broadcast tasked with injecting life into the program. He thought way outside the tackle box by bringing in Miller, a comedian known for arcane references and a run on “Saturday Night Live,” where he anchored “Weekend Update” from 1985 until 1991.
Miller’s stint on “MNF” is the subject of a new NFL Shorts documentary that premiered Sept. 29 on HBO called “Miller Night Football.”
The decision to hire him on “MNF” didn’t only catch the public off-guard, though.
“It was an honest reaction of ‘What?!,’ but I was a fan of Dennis,” Fouts, who is featured in the HBO documentary, tells TODAY.com.

“I was excited to meet him, but then figured out that this was kind of an experiment of Don Ohlmeyer’s to try to put something unique on the air for Monday night, kind of like the old days when they had Howard Cosell in the booth,” he says. “I think the idea was to have something that was a little controversial. So I was all onboard for it because it was ‘Monday Night Football.’”

Miller wasn’t a total neophyte in the broadcasting game. By the time he was hired, he had already won five Emmy Awards for his HBO series “Dennis Miller Live.” And while athletes had previously crossed over into the world of pop culture and news — TODAY’s Joe Garagiola, a former baseball player, was an early pioneer when he joined the show in 1967 — a comedian sliding into the booth on one of America’s most hallowed sports programs was unprecedented.
While headlines followed the hiring, Miller was not content to go for laughs just for the sake of getting them.

“I thought that Dennis came well prepared each week. He was excited about the job,” says Fouts, who started his run on “MNF” the same year Miller did and previously played quarterback for the San Diego Chargers between 1973 and 1987, making six Pro Bowls.

Panned by some, lauded by others, Miller’s presence in the booth provided renewed interest in “MNF,” as he had quips at the ready, oftentimes prepping them in advance, with Michael, Fouts and sideline reporter Melissa Stark.

“In Dennis’ mind, you know, he had things that he wanted to say, and he put him in there in his style, and it took awhile to figure out what the rhythm was,” Fouts says. “But once we got going … we got used to each other, and of course, having Al Michaels in the booth was the key because he’s the conductor of that train.”

As the documentary details, things changed in the second season, in 2001. Ohlmeyer left “MNF.” The Sept. 11 terror attacks put a pause on America’s appetite for laughter, several games were noncompetitive and Miller had studied the game to get more into Xs and Os. And then came the big development after the season ended: John Madden, considered the best analyst in the sport, was a free agent, with his contract at Fox running out. ABC came calling.
“He was available, and you just don’t turn down that opportunity to have the Babe Ruth of sports broadcasting,” Fouts says.
Without the confluence of events that preceded Miller and Fouts’ departure from “MNF,” could they and Michaels have continued?
“Oh, definitely,” Fouts says.

Fouts says he and Miller speak “once in a while” and “shared a few laughs” while talking to each other about the documentary. As he reflects a quarter of a century after his time with Miller and Michaels ended, he feels pride in playing a role in once again making “MNF” a water cooler show.
“Looking back at it, I think the documentary tells you that it was entertaining,” he said. “The goal was to bring the interest of ‘Monday Night Football’ back, and I certainly think it did that.”

title: Lindsay Lohan Recreates ‘Mean Girls’ Scene For A Most Fetch October 3rd
