summary: Lindsay Lohan, who played main character Cady Heron in “Mean Girls,” shared a video on social media, recreating the fan favorite scene in which Cady has an interaction with her school crush Aaron Samuels.
story: Attention all Plastics, Art Freaks, Preps and more — Lindsay Lohan is here to remind us that today’s the day.

The “Mean Girls” star, who played main character Cady Heron in the 2004 comedy, shared a video on social media, recreating the fan favorite scene in which Cady has an interaction with her school crush Aaron Samuels.
Though Jonathan Bennett, who played Aaron, isn’t featured in the clip, the video still sends us back to the early aughts.
The video shows Lohan sitting at a school desk behind another individual.
“On October 3rd, he asked me what day it was,” Lohan says in a voiceover that’s since become an internet classic.
“It’s October 3rd,” Lohan says in the clip just as she did in the film, before winking at the camera. Of course, it was posted on Oct. 3.

For years, the scene has been a source of internet fodder, with fans recreating it annually. It’s popularity has also given rise to what’s now known as “Mean Girls Day.” Lohan herself has observed the cult holiday in the past, posting stills from the famous scene on Oct. 3.
Comedian Tim Meadows, who played Principal Duvall in the comedy, released a skit just ahead of the holiday on social media in the form of a fake personal injury attorney ad.

“Sometimes it’s not easy to admit when you need help,” Meadows says in the skit, shared on Oct. 2. “It happened to me 20 years ago, but it feels like it was just yesterday. Every October 3rd is a reminder of her. Regina George.”
Attorney Mike Morse than asks the iconic question from the film, “Have you or anyone you know, ever felt personally victimized by Regina George?”
Regardless of whether Regina George ever punched you in the face (and it was awesome), here are some “Mean Girls” Day celebrations ideas.

title: Sarah Jessica Parker and Matthew Broderick’s Latest Date Night Looks Are Just Too Darling
summary: Celebrity couple Sarah Jessica Parker and Matthew Broderick attended the NYC Ballet Fall Fashion Gala at Lincoln Center together in Manhattan on Oct. 1.
story: This must be what that can’t-live-without-each-other love looks like!
Celebrity couple Sarah Jessica Parker and Matthew Broderick attended the NYC Ballet Fall Fashion Gala at Lincoln Center together in Manhattan on Oct. 1.
And just like that, the longtime married couple took fans’ breaths away with their stunning looks.

The “Sex and the City” star sported a sheer, pink tulle Simone Rocha dress that featured long, baby pink ribbons and floral accents. Her hair was styled in a long, voluminous braid down her back. A few ribbons were also incorporated into the dramatic braid.
Parker tied the outfit together with a bag that matched the shade of her dress, along with a pair glittering pointed-toe stilletos.
Broderick brought his own shine as he sported a classic black tux that was accented by a white flower lapel.

Parker, who has been married to Broderick since 1997, is the founding chair of the event, which was first established in 2012. It serves as an annual fundraiser for the NYC Ballet. Others big name attendees included legendary musician Stevie Nicks, the evening’s honorary chair and model Julia Fox, who served as a gala chair.
Fans, of course, had no chill over the stunning looks.
Several people on social media dubbed Parker “Rapunzel” for her long locks while others commented about the couple’s sweet poses as the two held hands amid several photos.
Parker and Broderick have three children together: son James Wilkie Broderick, born in October 2002, and twin daughters Tabitha Hodge Broderick and Marion Loretta Elwell Broderick, born in June 2009.
Parker, who met Broderick in 1991, told the New York Times that it was actually her brothers who had introduced her to her now-husband.
Broderick told “Watch What Happens Live” in 2022 that it didn’t take long for him to know that she was “the one.”
“Oh, the first time I met her,” Broderick told host Andy Cohen. “I saw her walking down the street and thought, ‘That’s it.’”

title: Ken Urker, Gypsy Rose Blanchard’s Boyfriend and Father of Her Daughter, Has Died
summary: More details have emerged after Gypsy Rose Blanchard’s partner and father of her daughter was found dead by police on Oct. 1 at a home in Louisiana.
story: More details have emerged after Gypsy Rose Blanchard’s partner and father of her daughter was found dead by police on Oct. 1 at a home in Louisiana.
The Lafourche Parish Sherriff’s Office issued an initial statement to NBC News Oct. 1 confirming that Ken Urker was found dead by deputies at a residence in Raceland, Louisiana. He was 34.

A preliminary report obtained by NBC News from the Lafourche Parish Sherriff’s Office on Oct. 2 calls the incident “drug related,” and the incident code is listed as “overdose.” Police said they found no signs of foul play.

According to the report, Blanchard’s half brother, Dylan Blanchard, and another person, Justin Daigle, told police they gained access to Urker’s unlocked bedroom window and entered the home after seeing Urker unconscious on his bed. Daigle told police Urker was “not breathing.”

Authorities were initially called by Anita Blanchard, who said that she and the two other men were trying to get access to Urker’s home because he had not been answering his phone or his front door, per the report.

Anita Blanchard, Dylan Blanchard and Daigle told the deputies when they arrived at the residence that Urker was dead, according to the report. Deputies entered the home and found syringes and a spoon in the bathroom next to “a brown powdery substance,” according to the report. They also located a syringe and a handgun on the nightstand next to the bed.
Urker had a paper towel placed on his left arm “with what appeared to be blotches of blood” on it, per the report.
Anita Blanchard and Dylan Blanchard told police Urker had made comments to them about being “depressed and upset” while with them at church on Sept. 30, according to the report.
Lafourche Parish Coroner Kayla Breaux said in a statement to NBC News that an autopsy was conducted Oct. 2 and “there is no definitive cause of death” at this time.

“The case remains pending completion of toxicology testing, and no further information regarding the cause of death will be available until those results are received and the investigation is complete,” Breaux said in the statement.

Gypsy Rose Blanchard told People magazine in an interview published Oct. 2 that Urker died of an overdose. TODAY has reached out to Blanchard as well as A+E Global Media, which owns Lifetime, the network that airs Blanchard’s reality show, “Gypsy Rose: Life After Lockup,” but did not immediately receive responses.

Blanchard and Urker first met when Blanchard was still in prison for her role in her allegedly abusive mother’s 2015 murder. The two got engaged in 2018 before they broke it off a year later. Blanchard was released from prison in 2023 after serving more than eight years of her 10-year sentence.
She and Urker eventually rekindled in 2024 and welcomed a daughter. In speaking to People on Oct. 2, Blanchard called Urker her soulmate.
“Ken was an amazing father and a man who was deeply loved,” she said. “He will forever be my soulmate and my red string, a connection that time, distance, and even death can never erase.”
In the time that she and Urker broke up, Blanchard married another man, Ryan Scott Anderson, in 2022. They separated in 2024 and finalized their divorce in December of that year.

Blanchard and Urker reconnected and announced in July 2024 that they were expecting a child together. They welcomed a baby girl, Aurora, on Dec. 28, 2024, just weeks after she finalized her divorce from Anderson.

“We honestly didn’t have a plan,” Blanchard told TODAY.com in March 2025. “It was really one of those things that we’re winging. So, whenever it comes to the scrutiny, we just hold true to each other. We lean on each other for support. One has to be the strong one, and then the other has a moment of rest and weakness to just let all of that sink in.”

Urker first connected with Blanchard in 2017, when he wrote a letter to her while she was an inmate at a Missouri state prison. He had learned about her story from watching “Mommy Dead and Dearest,” a 2017 HBO documentary about the murder of Blanchard’s mother, Clauddine “Dee Dee” Blanchard, as well as the abuse Blanchard suffered throughout her childhood.

Blanchard is thought to be a victim of Munchausen syndrome by proxy, a psychological disorder where a “caregiver feigns, exaggerates or induces illness in (another person) with the primary goal being to get attention, sympathy and praise,” Dr. Marc Feldman, a board-certified psychiatrist, said in a previous interview with TODAY.com.
Nicholas Godejohn, Blanchard’s ex-boyfriend who carried out the murder of her mother, is serving a life sentence without the possibility of parole after first pleading not guilty.
Blanchard was still in prison when Urker proposed to her in 2018. In August 2019, they broke it off.

“There were many adults in his life, presumably much ‘wiser’ than he, who suggested it wasn’t the right time for me to be married,” Blanchard explained in her 2024 memoir, “My Time to Stand.” “‘If you love her, you’ll set her free,’ was the common piece of advice he’d hear again and again, sometimes from prominent Hollywood therapists and other media personalities — sometimes from those in my own immediate family. I see now, he believed he was acting in my best interest by sacrificing his own needs and wants.”
Urker shared on Instagram in 2024 that the couple had gotten back together after Blanchard had separated from Anderson in 2022. The two then welcomed their daughter together later that year.

“My marriage with Ryan taught me a lot about myself,” Blanchard told TODAY.com. “There was something Ryan said in Season 1 (of ‘Gypsy Rose: Life After Lock Up’), ‘Life is not a fairy tale. It’s going to have its challenges.’ I didn’t understand that at the time. Now, after going through everything, I apply that to my relationship with Ken. We will have bad days, moments where we feel overwhelmed, but to not give up. Don’t just judge the whole relationship on that one day or that one argument.”

title: U.S. pressures European allies to release diesel reserves as Trump considers export ban
summary: The Trump administration asked European allies to release diesel from their emergency stockpiles to increase global supplies and tamp down on soaring prices.
story: The Trump administration ramped up a pressure campaign Thursday to persuade European allies to release diesel from national emergency stockpiles. The White House says additional diesel from Europe would increase global supplies and potentially keep a lid on soaring prices.
The average U.S. price of diesel has soared by 70% since the war with Iran began, hitting $6.38 per gallon Thursday, according to AAA.
Less than five weeks before the U.S. midterm elections, Republicans are eager for any way to lower domestic fuel prices.

“Our European partners should accelerate delivery on their existing commitments and make additional supplies immediately available to address ongoing disruptions” to energy markets, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Thursday on X.  “American farmers, truckers, and businesses should not be left carrying the burden of a global diesel shortage.”
Shortly after Bessent’s post, Trump told reporters “we may” request that Europe release some of its emergency reserves.
Earlier this week, U.S. Energy Secretary Chris Wright had appeared confident that Europe would agree to tap its reserves.

“You will hear announcements from our friends in Europe about new diesel supplies that’ll come to the market that’ll meaningfully push diesel prices down,” Wright told reporters Wednesday at an event with Trump in the Oval Office.
But as of Thursday evening, those announcements hadn’t materialized.

U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said he raised the diesel issue at a G20 trade ministers meeting in Milwaukee this week. But he did not suggest that Washington had gotten any firm commitments about emergency reserves.
“We’d love to have a collaborative response” to the global diesel crunch, he told Bloomberg News on Thursday.
Also in Milwaukee were trade ministers from China, India, the United Kingdom and other countries that have been affected by strained global diesel supplies.
So far, however, the message coming from Europe on diesel reserves is a noncommittal one.
The E.U. is “in very close contact with our member states on this ongoing issue,” European Commission energy spokesperson Anna-Kaisa Itkonen told reporters at a media briefing in Brussels.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
“We are also having high-level contacts ongoing with the U.S. administration,” she said.

The majority of Europe’s emergency diesel reserves are stored in Germany and France. Both American and European oil refineries have been running at near full capacity for months, churning out as much diesel fuel as possible.

While the Iran war is responsible for the lion’s share of price increases in crude oil and unleaded gasoline around the world, the price of diesel has been outpacing both of them since July, albeit for a different reason.
Russia has traditionally been a major exporter of diesel, but that stopped this summer after Ukrainian drone strikes destroyed Russian refineries.
On July 8, Russia banned the export of diesel in order to preserve its domestic supply. On Wednesday, the Kremlin extended that ban until the end of October.

“We’re tight on diesel because we’ve lost diesel exports from Russia,” Wright said at the White House. “We’ve lost diesel, some diesel exports from the Middle East, although we’re restoring those. And we’ve lost diesel exports from China.”
“That’s a lot of interruptions,” he said.

But whether Europe will tap its emergency reserves of diesel to increase global supply is complicated by the fact that the Trump administration is actively considering a move that is effectively the opposite of what it is asking Europe to do.
On Wednesday, the president mused about imposing a ban on exports of U.S. diesel.
“I’m thinking about it,” Trump told reporters in the Oval Office. “I speak to Chris and Doug about it a lot,” he said, referring to Wright and Interior Secretary Doug Burgum.
“They sort of think ... it’ll help diesel, but it might raise the price of other things,” he said.
An export ban on U.S. diesel would hit European countries particularly hard.
It would also land at a moment when average U.S. prices for unleaded gas remain almost 50% higher than they were on Feb. 28, the day the U.S. and Israel attacked Iran.

title: Russia says no plague found in contacts of Siberian lab worker who died
summary: News that a female staffer had died from a “pneumonia of undetermined” origin last week has spread fears worldwide.
story: Plague had not been detected among close contacts of a worker in an anti-plague laboratory in Siberia who died last week, with 60% of the identified group tested so far, officials in Russia said Tuesday.

News from Russia’s consumer and health watchdog Sunday that a female staffer at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Institute of Siberia and the Far East had died from a “pneumonia of undetermined” origin last week has raised public health fears worldwide.

“Laboratory testing identified two cases of Covid-19 and two cases of rhinovirus infection,” watchdog Rospotrebnadzor said in a statement, referring to the virus that causes the common cold. “No other infectious disease pathogens were detected among the contacts,” the statement said, without mentioning the word “plague.”
U.S. President Donald Trump said Tuesday he had a call scheduled with Russian President Vladimir Putin to discuss the matter.
Darya Shipilova, 28, was identified by her mother and Russian media outlets as the lab worker who died.

Regional and national Russian authorities have not confirmed that plague was involved in her death. However, a State Department spokesperson said Monday there had been “reports of a fatal case of suspected pneumonic plague” in Irkutsk oblast.

Separately, a State Department official told NBC News on Tuesday that the U.S. had been in contact with the Russian government as early as Friday. Health experts at the State Department had taken part in the contact along with the Russian Foreign Affairs Ministry, the official said.
The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention also said on X that it was “working across the U.S. government to assess developments as additional information becomes available.”
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
“At this time, there is no indication of a broader threat to the United States, but CDC and our interagency partners are prepared and will continue to monitor the situation closely,” it added.

The World Health Organization, which oversees global public health matters, said Tuesday that Russian health officials had informed it in response to its request about the lab worker’s death that no case of plague has been recorded in Irkutsk.
“According to the authorities, the woman’s illness initially presented as a typical acute respiratory viral infection,” it said.

No case of plague or other high-threat pathogen has reportedly been found among the woman’s close contacts, the WHO said, quoting the response from the Russian officials, adding that it’s awaiting confirmation from the Russian side about “what pneumonia-causing pathogen had led to the individual’s death.”

On Friday, Maksim Modin, mayor of the Shelekhov municipal district near the border with Mongolia, said that the inpatient facility where the worker is said to have been treated had been closed for quarantine. Russian media cited officials saying that nearly 200 people who had been in contact with the woman had been placed under precautionary medical observation.
Russian media outlets have named the woman and identified her as being 28 years old. These details have not been announced by officials.
Irkutsk’s governor, Igor Kobsev, said Monday that no “microorganisms linked to the employee’s professional activities were detected” in her body.

The Irkutsk regional branch of Rospotrebnadzor on Tuesday denied what it called “fake” reports circulating online that an “enhanced sanitary-epidemiological regime” and strict restrictions have been imposed in the region.
“No such decisions have been made at this time,” it said in a statement, saying the situation in the region remains stable.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Monday that even though there is “very limited travel between the U.S. and Russia,” if “something like that gets out, it could quickly spread.”
Rospotrebnadzor, the health watchdog, said Tuesday its probe found “no incidents involving the handling of pathogenic microorganisms.”
Trump told reporters Monday the United States would do what it could to help Russia.
“I hate to see them having it,” Trump said. “It’s a rough disease.”
Meanwhile, some of Russia’s neighbors have been stepping up preventive measures and quarantine controls at border crossings.
The Kremlin has called for those concerned to heed official statements.
“Rospotrebnadzor provides comprehensive information,” Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said when reporters pressed him about rumors spreading amid sparse official statements.
Peskov also deferred to Rospotrebnadzor when asked if the worker’s lab results would be released or if an autopsy has been conducted.

On its website, the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Institute of Siberia and the Far East says it was founded in 1934 “as a scientific and operational body for combating plague,” but over the years, its scope of responsibility expanded to include “other highly dangerous diseases,” including cholera and anthrax.
The institute says it’s a “multidisciplinary research and anti-epidemic facility” that helps ensure epidemic safety in the region.

title: U.S. resident charged with helping Canadian school shooter in rampage that killed 8
summary: Jesse Van Rootselaar, 18, killed her mother and stepbrother and then five students and a teacher at a secondary school in Tumbler Ridge, British Columbia, in February.
story: A 30-year-old Washington state resident was charged with providing assistance to a teenager who killed eight people in Canada, including schoolchildren, U.S. prosecutors said Tuesday.

James Cody Bryant, who the FBI said identifies as female, was arrested Tuesday and is charged with conspiracy to murder persons in a foreign country in connection with the Feb. 10 shootings in the British Columbia town of Tumbler Ridge, officials said.

Prosecutors said Bryant had been in contact over Discord with the shooter, who killed five children and a teacher at a secondary school, as well as two other people. He gave the shooter advice and money and offered to help livestream the killings, the U.S. Justice Department said.
Bryant “had been in repeated contact” with the shooter, the acting U.S. attorney for the Western District of Washington, Neil Floyd, said at a news conference Tuesday.

Bryant “had the information and ability to alert law enforcement, and even discussed that possibility with the shooter — but chose not to,” Floyd said. “Instead, he encouraged and offered assistance to a murderer.”

About 2 p.m. Feb. 10, Jesse Van Rootselaar, 18, who was born male but had been transitioning to female for six years, killed her mother and 11-year-old stepbrother in the small town of Tumbler Ridge, officials said.

She then went to Tumbler Ridge Secondary School and killed five children — three 12-year-old girls and two boys, one 12 and the other 13 — and a teacher, authorities said. Van Rootselaar then died by suicide.
The rampage was one of the deadliest shootings in Canada’s history. In addition to those who were killed, two other children were shot and seriously wounded, officials said.

Bryant tried to talk Van Rootselaar out of the attack or get her to reconsider several times but did not tell law enforcement about the plan and offered to livestream it, the U.S. Justice Department said.

The two met on the former random video chat service Omegle around three years before the shooting and kept in contact through Discord, an online communication service, said W. Mike Herrington, special agent in charge of the FBI’s Seattle office.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
There is no indication the two ever met in person, he said.

The back-and-forth messages on Discord cited in the complaint have a conversational and friendly tone. At one point, Bryant writes, “You believe me when I promise I won’t snitch on you, right?” At another point, Bryant tells Van Rootselaar, “if you are uncertain, maybe take it as a sign.”
On the day of the shootings, after Van Rootselaar killed her mother and stepbrother, she had trouble starting her car, Floyd said.
“Bryant provided advice and offered assistance on how to get the car started so that JVR could proceed to the school and kill children,” Floyd said, using the initials for the shooter’s name.
The charge of conspiracy to murder persons in a foreign country carries up to life in prison.
Bryant was in custody Tuesday, officials said. Online federal court records did not show an attorney representing Bryant on Tuesday afternoon.
The shooting was livestreamed on Twitch, but for only about 20 seconds before it shut off, officials said.
Twitch said an account appearing to be Bryant’s was the only account that saw it, according to the criminal complaint.
Herrington, of the FBI, said the shooter wanted maximum views but didn’t have much of a social media presence.

“Without Bryant’s misplaced loyalty and willingness to operate the livestream, we don’t ultimately know if the shooter would have gone through with the crime,” Herrington said. “We certainly know that the shooter was concerned that not enough people would see the livestream.”
Elija Rain, assistant commissioner of the British Columbia Royal Canadian Mounted Police, said the impact of the shooting was widespread.
“The people of Tumbler Ridge experienced a tragedy that forever changed the lives of families, friends, students, educators, first responders and the entire community,” he said.

title: What to know about pneumonic plague after woman in Russia dies from mysterious illness
summary: The death of a 28-year-old woman who worked in an anti-plague laboratory in Russia is raising concerns about what caused her illness.
story: The death of a 28-year-old woman who worked in an anti-plague laboratory in Russia is raising concerns about what caused her illness.

The woman died Friday, according to the World Health Organization, with no cause of death confirmed. A Russian official said the woman died of pneumonia of “undetermined” origin and did not link her death to her work at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Institute of Siberia and the Far East.
Darya Shipilova, 28, was identified by her mother and Russian media outlets as the lab worker.

On Tuesday, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention said on X that it is monitoring “reports of a suspected case of pneumonic plague in the Irkutsk region of Russia that resulted in a death,” although the circumstances of the case “remain unconfirmed.”

“At this time, there is no indication of a broader threat to the United States, but CDC and our interagency partners are prepared and will continue to monitor the situation closely,” the agency posted.

Key details aren’t known, including whether the woman was infected with plague at all and, if so, whether it was naturally occurring plague or bacteria studied in the lab. Scientists also don’t know how quickly her illness progressed and what treatment she received. Nearly 200 people who came into contact with the woman are under precautionary medical observation, according to Russian media.
Officials in Russia said Tuesday that no plague had been detected in 60% of the identified group tested so far.

“Maybe it’s going to come out that she died from something unrelated and it was just a coincidence” that she worked in an anti-plague lab, said Lisa Morici, a microbiologist and immunologist in the Tulane University School of Medicine.

Dr. Ashish Jha, the White House’s former Covid response coordinator, told NBC News in an interview, “If there were weapons programs, biological weapons programs in these labs, that would be much more concerning to me.”
“We need to understand that now,” he added.
The situation is still rapidly unfolding. But here’s what we know about the pneumonic plague, how it spreads and how dangerous it is.
What is plague?

Plague is an infection caused by Yersinia pestis bacteria. Known as the “Black Death” during the 14th century, the plague triggered several global pandemics over centuries before the discovery of antibiotics.
It presents in three main forms: bubonic, pneumonic and septicemic, according to the World Health Organization. All three are caused by Yersinia pestis, but they occur in different parts of the body.

Bubonic is the most common form, Morici said. It is primarily transmitted through bites of infected fleas or direct contact with infected rodents, which can cause painful, swollen lumps in the lymph nodes. It is usually not contagious.
Left untreated, however, it can spread to the lungs and become pneumonic plague, which can pass from person to person through respiratory droplets, Morici said.
Septicemic plague occurs when the bacteria grow and spread in the blood.
How does pneumonic plague spread?
Pneumonic plague can spread through the air when an infected person or animal coughs or sneezes.

The respiratory droplets don’t travel very far, maybe three to six feet, said Dr. Dave Wagner, director of the Pathogen and Microbiome Institute at Northern Arizona University. “They drop to the ground pretty quickly.”
It’s the rarest form of the disease, according to WHO.

Dr. William Schaffer, an infectious diseases expert at Vanderbilt University Medical Center, said close contacts are most at risk. Pneumonic plague isn’t something that spreads “distantly across a room, but to face-to-face contacts,” he said.
“It’s highly unlikely for most people to get the pneumonic form of the disease,” Morici said.
Covid, for example, spreads like wildfire through the air, traveling beyond six feet.
“It’s nothing like the Covid-19 pandemic,” she said.
How deadly is it?
While pneumonic plague is the rarest form of the disease, it’s also the deadliest.
“It’s the one that’s so frightening because it can kill so quickly,” Morici said.

It progresses remarkably fast, Wagner said. Symptoms typically appear within one to two days of exposure, and patients require treatment within 48 hours of showing symptoms to prevent fatal complications. Symptoms can include shortness of breath and coughing or blood in the phlegm.
Because of how rapidly it attacks the respiratory system, public health experts consider this strain the most likely candidate for a biological attack, according to Morici.

People with pneumonic plague are often quarantined, she said. Healthcare workers will often wear personal protective equipment, such as an N95 mask, or even a full body suit in case of accidental exposure.
“We’re using the strictest levels of biocontainment,” she said.
How is it treated?
Antibiotics are highly effective against plague, including pneumonic plague.
“This is why we don’t have big plague outbreaks anymore,” Wagner said.
Are experts worried about a potential plague outbreak?

Schaffner said there’s no evidence to suggest that the plague bacteria are evolving in a way to become resistant to antibiotics. “We will not turn 2026 into the Middle Ages, where the Black Death caused vast amounts of death throughout Europe. That will not happen.”
Wagner said he has no reason to believe this suspected case of plague is “going to take off and spread.”
“The plague that we have today is the same plague that was the scourge of humanity for so long during great pandemics,” he said.
Is the plague found in the U.S.?

About seven cases of plague are reported in the U.S. each year, according to the CDC. Most occur in rural parts of the Southwest, including Arizona, California, Colorado and New Mexico. These are areas where Yersinia pestis bacteria naturally circulate among wild rodents like prairie dogs and their fleas.
Most people are treated quickly with antibiotics and recover. Deaths from the plague in the U.S. are rare but do happen.

Last July, a man in Arizona died of pneumonic plague after he was exposed to sick cats. Within a week, the man went to an emergency department with shallow breathing, a fast heart rate, chest pain and a dry cough. Despite getting antibiotics and oxygen, the man died within eight hours of his admission to the hospital. Testing later showed he had pneumonic plague.

title: Flydubai pilot planned a 9/11-style attack on Tel Aviv airport, source says
summary: The suspect was being questioned by investigators in the United Arab Emirates.
story: TEL AVIV — The pilot accused of trying to bring down an Israel-bound flight had been planning a 9/11-style attack by crashing into the country’s main airport in Tel Aviv, a Middle Eastern official has told NBC News.

The pilot, identified by NBC News as Hamman al-Hamammi, told investigators Monday that he wanted to evade Israel’s defenses and crash into the Ben Gurion Airport or another building, said the official, who spoke on condition of anonymity because the person was not authorized to speak publicly.
Multiple sources from three agencies briefed on the investigation and a diplomat in the Middle East identified al-Hammami, an Omani citizen. Authorities have not officially released the identity.

He is currently being questioned by investigators in the United Arab Emirates after he was transferred from Saudi Arabia. The flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv was diverted to an airport in Saudi Arabia, where it landed safely, after last week’s dramatic midair incident.
Emirati authorities said Saturday that the pilot attacked his fellow pilot, Capt. Smit Machchhar, with a crash ax and tried to take control of the aircraft’s flight controls.

The jet, which was carrying 174 passengers, most of them Israeli, then plummeted 14,000 feet in just 29 seconds, according to data from the aviation tracking service Flightradar24, causing panic onboard.

Machchhar, an Indian national and a veteran pilot of 17 years, said in a call Friday with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu that his fellow pilot told him he was going to pray, something he didn’t consider unusual as observant Muslims pray five times a day.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

A few minutes later, he said he felt a strong blow to the head. “Because of his initial blows, my vision was almost like nothing, and I was completely blurred out,” he added. “The next feeling that I had was that the aircraft was sharply going down.”
A video of the call was released by Netanyahu’s office.

Initially, Machchhar said, he thought there was “catastrophic damage to the aircraft,” but once the blows kept coming, he “realized that it’s not the aircraft, it’s the other guy who was in the cockpit with me.”
In a separate call with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, also Friday, Machchhar said he managed to open the cockpit’s door on the second attempt, despite the blows raining down.
“I gave everything that I had and just went for the door and opened the door. And thankfully, people were waiting to pounce back,” he said.
Focus has shifted onto the missed security signals ahead of the flight.

Citing sources familiar with the matter, The Wall Street Journal reported Saturday that al-Hammami had “previously been banned from flying by Oman over concerns he had adopted radical ideological views.”
It is unclear how a citizen of Oman, an Arab country with no diplomatic relations with Israel, was allowed to fly the plane carrying Israelis to Tel Aviv.
According to Israeli law, airlines must provide information about passengers and crew members, including their names and nationalities, up to 48 hours before a flight.

Israeli investigators are leaning toward the assessment that the pilot was acting as a lone wolf, according to an Israeli official and a source familiar with the matter, although they said there is still more to learn about what led to his radicalization.
In the meantime, Netanyahu has called on the head of the National Security Council to appoint an examiner to review “all security aspects” of Israel’s civil aviation in the aftermath of the incident.
Elsewhere, Vice President JD Vance underlined the concerns about potential security failures.

“That person should not have been flying an airline, and so we’re certainly looking at our procedures within the United States to make sure that people who are obviously flight risks are not getting behind the wheel of an airplane,” he told a reporter at Joint Base Andrews, Maryland, on Monday.

title: Iranian drone threat prompted U.S. to remove bombers from British base, officials say
summary: The bombers at RAF Fairford “have been re-deployed to their home stations in the United States,” a Pentagon official told NBC News.
story: WASHINGTON — Reports about a possible Iranian drone attack prompted the U.S. Air Force to remove its bombers from a British air base it used to strike the Islamic Republic, two U.S. officials said Monday.

The officials could not say whether the Iranian threat was imminent. A third U.S. official said America can deploy the bombers from anywhere, so it made sense to move them out of an abundance of caution.
The move from RAF Fairford also came in the wake of an investigation into a possible planned terrorist attack at the base.
A Defense Department official told NBC News that “all U.S. bombers that were deployed to RAF Fairford have re-deployed to their home stations in the United States.”
“U.S. Air Force bombers routinely operate around the world to support global force readiness and operational requirements,” the official said.

“The Airmen that operate America’s bomber force, including B-1s, B-2s, and B-52s, remain ready to deliver precision global strike capabilities — including through operations that launch and recover from the continental United States — anywhere, anytime,” the official added.
The rushed withdrawal of at least 12 bombers included several that had just arrived in the U.K. as part of a rotation to the air base, two Pentagon officials told NBC News.

Those officials said the hasty deployment back to the U.S. was not a response to a new or different threat to the U.K. base but rather part of the threat reporting that was already out there, without giving further detail.
The United Kingdom’s Defense Ministry declined to comment on the matter Monday.

title: BA flight to Chicago drops 28,000 feet, returns to London
summary: About 30 minutes into its journey, the aircraft dropped from 36,000 feet to 9,000 feet in around seven minutes, according to flight-tracking website FlightAware.
story: LONDON — A British Airways passenger jet flying from London to Chicago descended 28,000 feet in just seven minutes after declaring an emergency due to an unspecified “technical issue,” the airline said Monday.
The Boeing 777 took off at 12:15 p.m. local time (7:15 a.m. ET) but started descending just 30 minutes later while flying over Ireland, according to flight-tracking website FlightAware.

The plane turned around and spent around four hours zigzagging over the Bristol Channel, a waterway to the west of England, before landing back at London Heathrow Airport at 5 p.m. local time (noon ET).

“The aircraft landed safely after our highly-trained pilots returned to Heathrow following a technical issue,” British Airways said in an emailed statement. “Customers disembarked the aircraft normally and our teams are working to get their travel plans back on track as quickly as possible.”
Heathrow did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
Passengers will likely be put up in hotels by the airline until another flight can be arranged, as stipulated by the U.K. Civil Aviation Authority.

Britain’s National Air Traffic Service (NATS) came under scrutiny last month after two technical problems in the space of two weeks caused major delays at several U.K. airports and hundreds of flights were canceled.
NATS blamed software issues for the delays.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
Britain’s Transport Secretary Heidi Alexander acknowledged the situation had been “deeply frustrating” for passengers.
With 84.5 million passengers last year, Heathrow ranked seventh in the table of the world’s busiest airports, according to data published by Airports Council International.
Travel from Heathrow was severely disrupted in March last year when a massive fire at an electricity substation caused a predawn power outage at the global transport hub.
The closure affected more than 1,300 flights and 200,000 passengers.

After investigating 600 items of evidence related to the substation, the National Energy System Operator ruled out suspicious activity in a report saying a preventable moisture fault caused the fire, leaving almost 70,000 homes without power.

title: 200 people enter medical observation after worker at Russian anti-plague lab dies
summary: The female staffer at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Institute of Siberia and the Far East died from a “pneumonia of undetermined” origin last week, according to a regional governor.
story: The death of a worker at an anti-plague laboratory in Russia has prompted officials to put at least one hospital facility under quarantine and nearly 200 people reportedly under medical observation as of Monday.
The female staffer at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Institute of Siberia and the Far East died from a “pneumonia of undetermined” origin last week, according to the regional governor, Igor Kobsev.
He said no “microorganisms linked to the employee’s professional activities were detected” in her body, and that there had been “no new cases” of illness among other employees of the lab.
“The sanitary-epidemiological situation” in the area “is currently stable,” Kobsev said.

On Friday, Maksim Modin, mayor of the Shelekhov municipal district near the border with Mongolia, said that the inpatient facility where the worker is said to have been treated had been closed for quarantine. Russian media cited officials saying that nearly 200 people who had been in contact with the woman had been placed under precautionary medical observation.
Russian media outlets have named the woman and identified her as being 28 years old. These details have not been confirmed by officials.
Meanwhile, there have been calls internationally for more information and greater transparency from Moscow.

“Many details have not been confirmed,” a State Department spokesman said. “We encourage Russian authorities to share accurate information quickly and openly.” The spokesman said there had been “reports of a fatal case of suspected pneumonic plague” in Irkutsk oblast.
For Subscribers

Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Monday that even though there is “very limited travel between the U.S. and Russia,” if “something like that gets out, it could quickly spread.” So the U.S. government is “watching and monitoring it closely,” he added. “I don’t think it’s cause for alarm, but it is cause for focus and a cause just to keep an eye on it.”
The World Health Organization said in a statement that it was aware of reports that a lab worker had died of “severe pneumonia” but that “no cause of death has been officially confirmed.”
For Subscribers

Asked by NBC News in Moscow whether the Kremlin was following these events, President Vladimir Putin’s spokesman, Dmitry Peskov, said Rospotrebnadzor, Russia’s consumer welfare service, was handling the investigation.

“It is their official statements that should be relied upon — rather than paying heed to various rumors, speculations and the like,” he said. “Rospotrebnadzor employs highly qualified professionals in this field, so let us heed their official statements.”

Dr. Ashish Jha, the White House’s former Covid response coordinator, told NBC News that “much more” information and transparency were needed from Moscow. He said that if this is an isolated case of pneumonic plague and no one else dies, “it will probably end there.”

But “it’s actually very hard” for pneumonic plague to spread from person to person, Jha said. “We may see a few more people get infected, but the chances that this becomes a larger outbreak, let alone a global pandemic, is exceedingly low,” he said.
“If there were weapons programs, biological weapons programs in these labs, that would be much more concerning to me,” he said. “We need to understand that now.”

The pneumonic plague is caused by the same bacteria as the bubonic plague and can spread from person to person through airborne respiratory droplets, typically from sneezing or coughing. Medical experts say cases require rapid treatment with powerful antibiotics to prevent fatalities.

From 2019 to 2025, 10 countries reported more than 3,800 suspected human plague cases to the WHO, the agency said last week. Six of the countries ended up having confirmed cases, most of them in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Madagascar, with 423 deaths.

title: Russia pounds Kyiv during German chancellor’s visit in a new escalation
summary: Germany’s foreign intel chief warns it could become embroiled in a conflict with Russia as Moscow steps up its “shadow war” against European democracies.
story: Germany’s leader faced a grim new reality as his train pulled into Kyiv: air raid sirens and the boom of Russian strikes on the Ukrainian capital.

During previous visits by international dignitaries of Chancellor Friedrich Merz’s stature, the Kremlin paused or dramatically reduced attacks on the city. On Sunday, the sounds of war rang out repeatedly as the German delegation made its way around Kyiv, in what looks to be a new level of escalation by Moscow.

On Monday, Germany’s foreign intelligence chief warned his country was at risk of becoming embroiled in a “violent conflict with Russia,” as Moscow steps up its “shadow war” against European democracies.

Germany has been one of the most ardent supporters of Ukraine since the early days of the Russian invasion, supplying both military and financial aid. The country has also taken in more than a million Ukrainian refugees fleeing the war.
Add to Google
Add to Google

Merz’s visit came as Russia has ramped up its around-the-clock strikes on Kyiv in recent weeks. The attacks and the air raid alerts that accompany them have severely disrupted life in the city, forcing millions to constantly seek shelter and paralyzing the capital’s businesses and transport networks.

Over the last four days, including on the day Merz was visiting, Russia has hit several of Kyiv’s key bridges, with some strikes coming in broad daylight and as traffic was flowing through them — in what appears to be a new tactic to disrupt links between the capital’s two sides separated by the Dnipro River to further disable movement around Ukraine’s largest city.

An air raid alert went off as Merz and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy visited the site of a drone attack on the National Academy of Sciences last week. The dramatic daytime strike on the national landmark saw people clinging to windows to escape flames and thick smoke billowing out of the structure.

title: Early indications suggest Flydubai co-pilot acted alone in attack, officials say
summary: Officials cautioned that the investigation remains in its early stages and that possible links to an organization or foreign government haven’t been definitively ruled out.
story: TEL AVIV — Early indications suggest the Flydubai co-pilot accused of attacking his captain and trying to seize control of an Israel-bound plane acted alone, rather than as part of a larger organization or on behalf of a foreign government, multiple U.S. officials briefed on the investigation and a former Israeli security official told NBC News.
The U.S. officials cautioned that the investigation into Wednesday’s midair attack remains at an early stage.

“The assessment is that he operated alone. Right now, it looks like a case of ‘lone wolf’ terrorism inspired by content found online,” said Shalom Ben Hanan, a former official in the Shin Bet, Israel’s domestic security agency.
“We still need to wait for the final investigation results to determine whether an organization or a state is behind it,” he added.

Emirati authorities, who are leading the investigation, said Saturday that the co-pilot attacked the captain with a crash ax and attempted to take control of the aircraft’s flight controls in an attempted terrorist attack.

The flight was carrying 174 mostly Israeli passengers from Dubai to Tel Aviv. A crash was averted when crew members and passengers entered the cockpit and subdued the attacker, according to eyewitnesses and Israeli officials.

NBC News has identified the suspect as Omani citizen Hamam al-Hammami, based on information from multiple sources from three agencies briefed on the investigation and a diplomat in the Middle East. Authorities have not released his identity.
UAE Attorney General Hamad Saif Al Shamsi said Saturday that investigators were working to establish the incident’s “full circumstances, motives, and any links.”
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
The preliminary assessment comes after Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said Friday that investigators were examining whether the attacker had been sent by someone.

President Donald Trump also raised the possibility of Iranian involvement Thursday, threatening renewed strikes against Iran if it was behind the attack. A senior U.S. official briefed on the Israeli investigation previously told NBC News there were no indications that Iran directed or was involved in the attack.

The flight captain, Indian national Smit Machchhar, said Friday from a hospital in Abu Dhabi that he had been severely injured and could sense the aircraft descending before he managed to open the cockpit door, allowing passengers and crew to intervene.
“I was acting for my own life, but at the same time, I knew I couldn’t let all of them die,” he said on a video call released by India’s Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
Raf Sanchez and Paul Goldman reported from Tel Aviv and Tom Winter from New York.

title: U.S. Marine arrested on suspicion of killing Japanese woman in Okinawa
summary: Japan’s Defense Ministry said it was “deeply outraged by the extremely brutal and heinous crime committed by a U.S. Marine.”
story: A U.S. service member is in custody on suspicion of killing a Japanese national on the island of Okinawa.

Lance Cpl. Devin Jacob Ballard, 20, is suspected of killing Anna Yagi, 39, in a hotel in Naha, the capital of the southernmost prefecture, on Saturday and taking her wallet and backpack, ​local police told the Reuters news agency. Ballard denied the allegations, police said.
The Marine was stationed at Futenma Air Station on Okinawa Island, police said, adding that he was arrested at 1 a.m. local time Sunday.

“An investigation is underway to determine the facts of the case, the United States is communicating and cooperating with the Government of Japan and local authorities,” the U.S. Embassy in Tokyo said Sunday on X.
Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi described the death as an alleged robbery and murder.

“The occurrence of such an extremely brutal and heinous incident is a matter of profound regret, and as the Government of Japan, we have lodged a strong protest with the U.S. side,” she said on social media.
Japan’s Defense Ministry said it was “deeply outraged by the extremely brutal and heinous crime committed by a U.S. Marine.”
It said on X that it had made “a firm demand for stricter discipline, thorough measures to prevent recurrence.”

The III Marine Expeditionary Force, a combat force of the U.S. Marine Corps headquartered in Okinawa, said it was cooperating with Japanese authorities in response to “allegations of serious criminal actions by a Marine.”
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

“The Marine Corps takes these allegations very seriously and expects every Marine to adhere to the highest standards of behavior,” it posted on X. “The Marine is in custody of local authorities while investigations proceed.”
Approached for further comment, the Pentagon referred NBC News to the Marines’ statement.
U.S. Ambassador to Japan George Glass said he had spoken with Japan’s Foreign Affairs Ministry and Okinawa Gov. Genta Koja, “pledging full cooperation as the investigation continues.”

There are 18,000 U.S. Marines based in Japan, the majority of them stationed in Okinawa, just 60 miles from Taiwan at its closest point. The U.S. held the island from the end of World War II until 1972, and the presence of the U.S. military has often stirred resentment among residents.

The 1995 abduction and rape of a 12-year-old girl by three U.S. servicemen sparked mass protests, as tens of thousands of people took to the streets, forcing Washington and Tokyo to discuss ways to reduce the U.S. military presence on the island.

title: Flydubai pilot attacked captain with cockpit’s crash ax in attempted terrorist act, UAE official says
summary: TEL AVIV — A Flydubai pilot attacked his flight captain using a crash ax and tried to take control of the aircraft’s controls in an attempted terrorist attack, an official with the United Arab Emirates said Saturday.
story: TEL AVIV — A Flydubai pilot attacked his flight captain using a crash ax and tried to take control of the aircraft’s controls in an attempted terrorist attack, an official with the United Arab Emirates said Saturday.

The suspect is Omani citizen Hamam al-Hammami, multiple sources from three agencies briefed on the investigation and a diplomat in the Middle East told NBC News. Authorities have not officially released the identity.
The Wall Street Journal, citing sources familiar with the matter, reported that al-Hammami had “previously been banned from flying by Oman over concerns he had adopted radical ideological views.”
Oman Air did not immediately respond to a request for comment on whether he previously worked for the company.

Emirati officials are leading investigations into the midair incident, which occurred Wednesday on a flight carrying 174 mostly Israeli passengers from Dubai to Tel Aviv. A crash was averted, according to eyewitnesses and Israeli officials, when crew and passengers were able to enter the cabin and subdue the attacker.

“Investigations into the incident aboard Flydubai flight FZ1073 revealed that the co-pilot attempted to carry out a terrorist act,” UAE Attorney General Hamad Saif Al Shamsi said in an update on Saturday.
“The co-pilot began executing his plan during the flight, attacking the captain inside the flight deck using a crash axe and attempting to take control of the aircraft’s flight controls,” he said.
Al-Hammami was transferred from Saudi Arabia to Abu Dhabi on Thursday, the Saudi Interior Ministry said. The statement said his health had “improved,” but his medical condition was unclear.
Al Shamsi said investigations were ongoing to “establish the full circumstances, motives, and any links related to the incident.”

Israeli government spokesman David Mencer said Friday that Israeli investigators would “join their Emirati counterparts in investigating this attempted mass murder and establishing precisely what happened, his motives and background.”

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said Friday: “As time passes, the picture becomes clearer: The attacker had undergone Islamist radicalization. He came to crash the plane, along with its passengers.”
He did not say how he reached that conclusion, but added: “We are investigating whether he was sent, and whoever sent him will pay a very heavy price.”
Netanyahu’s spokesman Doron Spielman told NBC News that the suspect “talks on his social media about killing Jews.”
The flight captain, Indian national Capt. Smit Machchhar, spoke for the first time Friday from a hospital in Abu Dhabi.
Flydubai pilot speaks out follow mid-air attack
Machchhar was widely praised for his efforts to prevent the plane from crashing by opening the cockpit door and allowing passengers and crew members to rush in.
Speaking from his hospital bed, Machchhar said he had been “severely injured” and “could sense that the aircraft was going down.”

“I was acting for my own life, but at the same time, I knew I couldn’t let all of them die,” he said on a video call released by India’s Prime Minister Narendra Modi, adding that he told himself to “give just one last push” to the cockpit door.
The Indian Embassy in Abu Dhabi called Machchhar the “Indian braveheart,” saying in an X post Saturday that he “remains under excellent medical care & is recovering well.”

The deputy prime minister of the United Arab Emirates, Hamdan bin Mohammed, posted photos on X after visiting Machchhar in the hospital in which he’s seen kissing the pilot’s head and shaking his hand. Machchhar, with one arm in a cast and medical dressings on his head, appears awake and smiling.
“From us, and from the leadership of the nation, he has our full appreciation and praise,” he wrote.
Ayelet Epstein, a 47-year-old Israeli, told NBC News that her 14-year-old daughter asked if they were going to die when they heard shouting and “a huge fall started.”
“I told her, no, I don’t think so, we’re going to be OK,” she said, adding that “I was trying to rationalize things in a hopeful way for her.”
Epstein thanked Machchhar “from the bottom of my heart” for saving their lives, lauding his bravery.

A Flydubai spokesperson said Saturday: “We recognise that there are many questions at this stage; however, the circumstances surrounding the incident are still under investigation. We are therefore not in a position to comment further beyond our published statements.”
“We remain fully committed to supporting the ongoing investigation and are in close coordination with the relevant government authorities and regulators,” the spokesperson added.
President Donald Trump told reporters Thursday that there would be renewed strikes against Iran if it was behind the attack.
“You just ask them,” he said. “They know what happened. They’ll be hit very hard.”
There are no indications that Iran directed or was involved in the attack, a senior U.S. official briefed on the Israeli investigation told NBC News.
Raf Sanchez and Shira Pinson reported from Tel Aviv. Freddie Clayton reported from London. Tom Winter and Jonathan Dienst reported from New York.

title: Two Iranian nationals charged over alleged terrorism plot targeting Jewish community in England
summary: British police said Friday that they had charged two Iranian nationals accused of plotting a terrorist attack against the Jewish community in Manchester on the eve of Yom Kippur, the holiest day in the Jewish calendar.
story: British police said Friday that they had charged two Iranian nationals accused of plotting a terrorist attack against the Jewish community in Manchester on the eve of Yom Kippur, the holiest day in the Jewish calendar.
Rahman Salehi, 34, and Salam Ahmadyan, 36, were charged with “engaging in conduct in preparation for terrorist acts” on or before September 20, according to a British police statement.
The two men had allegedly been in contact with an overseas third-party who might be in Iran in relation to the plot, the Metropolitan Police said.
Salehi and Ahmadyan had components for manufacturing an improvised explosive device and conducted reconnaissance for potential targets, according to the statement.

On Monday, police arrested five British nationals in connection with a massive security operation near a base used by the U.S. Air Force to facilitate strikes on Iran, the counterterrorism officials running the operation said.

The five men, all from London and in their early to mid-20s, were arrested Sunday on suspicion of terrorism and explosives offenses after three suspicious vehicles were seen moving toward RAF Fairford, a Royal Air Force station about 90 minutes west of London.
The men were released on bail, but police arrested a dual U.K.-Iranian national Thursday in relation to the incident.
For Subscribers
Prime Minister Andy Burnham said Wednesday there are strong indications that Tehran played a part in the security incident outside the air base.
For Subscribers
Iran has denied any involvement.
Vicki Evans, the senior national coordinator for counterterrorism policing, said the alleged plot in Manchester was not linked to the incident at the airbase.

“This week also brought into sharp focus some of the wider threats being projected into the UK from Iran,” Evans said in the statement. “While this incident and the investigation into the RAF Fairford incident are not connected in any way, I want to reassure the public that CTP, working with our national security partners, are using the full range of our capabilities to protect the UK from any hostile acts.”

title: Screaming, panicking, blood: Passengers detail horrifying Israel-bound flight
summary: It was too early to say why a pilot stabbed another on the flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv, according to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
story: TEL AVIV — A stabbing, an emergency alert, a terrifying midair plunge.
Details are still emerging after an Israel-bound flight carrying 180 people emitted a distress signal Wednesday, raising fears of a possible hijacking when one pilot stabbed the other in the cockpit.
Aviatar Alevi, who was on the Flydubai flight Wednesday, described people “screaming, running, panicking, blood.”
“At the start, I thought it was a plane malfunction, but then I started hearing screaming about the stabbings,” Alevi, 17, told NBC News. “Then I understood the weight of the actual situation.”
“We didn’t know what was going to happen,” he said, adding that the possibility of death “was definitely an option.”
The plane made an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia, one of its rudders damaged, apparently by the force of its descent.
The passengers, who had been flying from Dubai, were mobbed by media and flag-waving fellow Israelis after they finally arrived at Ben Gurion Airport near Tel Aviv.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
They said they feared for their lives after the plane plunged more than 14,000 feet in 29 seconds at one point, according to FlightRadar24.
“Imagine sitting on the plane, all scared after you fell down five kilometers. You don’t understand anything,” 16-year-old Peleg Itali told NBC News.

Capt. Smit Machchhar, an Indian national, was recovering in a hospital in Saudi Arabia on Thursday as the other pilot, so far identified only as an Omani citizen, was being interrogated elsewhere in the country. Machchhar was widely praised for his efforts to prevent the plane from crashing, opening the cockpit door and allowing passengers and crewmembers to rush in.

Machchhar and the pilot who initiated the attack were transferred to Abu Dhabi, the capital of the United Arab Emirates, on Thursday, the Saudi Arabian Interior Ministry said in a statement, citing an unnamed “official source” at the ministry.

“The source indicated that initial investigations conducted by the competent authorities in the Kingdom, with the participation of a security team from the sisterly United Arab Emirates, revealed an assault on the pilot by his co-pilot, resulting in both sustaining various injuries,” the ministry said. “The source confirmed that the pilot and his co-pilot, after their health improved and the medical team cleared them, departed the Kingdom for Abu Dhabi this morning.”
Few details had emerged about the pilot Thursday morning. Questions about a possible motive, including whether it was terrorism-related, hang over the attack.

“I don’t think it was a hijacking. It looks like a suicide attempt, simply because of what this hero, Yaniv, has described,” Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on “CBS Evening News” as he praised Yaniv Hayun, who rushed into the cockpit and subdued the attacker.
Hayun, who was pictured with his shirt spattered with blood sitting next to Netanyahu, said he confronted the pilot who initiated the attack, according to the Israeli government press office.
“I grabbed the attacker and choked him, pulled him out first,” Hayun said. “I started pulling the controls.”
“Thank God, we pulled it off. We really put our heads together and worked as a team,” Hayun said, adding: “It was between fear and a sense of a do-or-die situation.”
“We had to win. We had to pull through and come out on top,” he said. Hayun told Netanyahu that he acted based on what he had seen on a TV show and helped stabilize the plane.
Flydubai said on-duty crewmembers on the flight were able to land the plane.
Motive under investigation
Netanyahu said it was still too early to determine why the pilot apparently stabbed his colleague and appeared to try to take over the Flydubai flight and whether Iran was involved.

“We’ve had signs that Iran, in particular through its proxies, was intending to heighten terrorist attacks against Israel and Israeli nationals abroad,” he said. “But I think it’s too early to say whether there was Iranian collusion here.”
Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz branded the incident a “jihadist terrorist attack attempt,” without expanding on how he had reached that conclusion.
President Donald Trump also weighed in, calling it “an incredible story.”
“It seems as though the co-pilot was perhaps a terrorist or perhaps a whack job, and he stabbed the pilot,” Trump told reporters.
On Thursday, Trump told reporters at the White House that the pilot who initiated the attack could be linked to Iran.
“I would say the answer, based on what I’m hearing, is yes. But we’re working on it right now,” he said.
Asked whether the pilot could have been radicalized or working with Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, Trump replied, “Could have been, yeah.”
Trump also told reporters Thursday that there would be renewed strikes against Iran if it was behind the attack.
“Oh, they’ll be hit very hard, don’t worry,” he said.
“You just ask them,” he added. “They know what happened. They’ll be hit very hard.”
All the passengers were Israeli, according to Netanyahu’s office. Four were dual American-Israeli citizens, two U.S. officials told NBC News.

With few details about the suspect or any potential motive surrounding the incident, Doron Spielman, a spokesperson for Netanyahu’s office, said there was a “strong opinion” that the incident was a terrorist attack, “but we can’t be sure until we debrief everybody.”
An investigation by Saudi authorities is ongoing, David Mencer, a spokesperson for the Israeli Prime Minister’s Office, said separately.
A senior U.S. official and a Saudi official who were both briefed on the Israeli investigation said the stabbing increasingly looked like an act of terrorism based on early findings.
The United Arab Emirates’ attorney general, Hamad Saif Al Shamsi, separately ordered an investigation.

His office said the probe would seek to “gather information and evidence, establish the facts and circumstances of the incident, and determine the underlying motives,” in addition to examining “whether the incident was linked to any terrorist activity or purpose, or involved any prior planning or direction.”

Hessa Alyahya, spokesperson for the Saudi Embassy in the U.S., said authorities were waiting to determine whether the attack was a dispute between the pilots or whether it was an act sponsored by Iran or the Houthis.
Israel and Saudi Arabia do not have official diplomatic relations.

title: What we know about the cockpit stabbing on Israel-bound flight
summary: What we know about the potential midair disaster aboard the Flydubai flight when a pilot attacked his colleague causing the plane to plunge thousands of feet.
story: Questions remain about how a pilot managed to sneak a weapon aboard a plane and stab his fellow pilot before it plunged thousands of feet in mere seconds. The attacker was thwarted, passengers said, and the plane made an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia.
“We were so scared. We didn’t know what was going to happen,” Aviatar Alevi, a 17-year-old student, told NBC News on Wednesday after he and the rest of the passengers were flown to Tel Aviv.
Here is what we know about the incident and how close it came to resulting in tragedy.
What did passengers see?
Alevi described a harrowing scene aboard the flight, with people “screaming, running, panicking, blood.”
“At the start, I thought it was a plane malfunction, but then I started hearing screaming about the stabbings,” he said.
“We didn’t know what was going to happen,” he said, adding that the possibility of death “was definitely an option.”
Another passenger, Motti Cohen Or, 70, said that he heard a woman shouting that “someone is stabbing someone in the cockpit” before the aircraft dived “toward the ground.”
Yaniv Hayun was pictured in a bloody T-shirt telling cameras he had been among those to enter the cockpit and subdue the attacking pilot.
At Ben Gurion Airport, after the passengers had returned to Israel, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu thanked Hayun, whom he later identified as a plumber.

Three others helped in the effort to save the plane and those aboard, Hayun told reporters. The group struggled to open the cockpit door. “I grabbed the attacker, and choked him, pulled him out first,” he said. “I started pulling the controls.”
“Thank God, we pulled it off. We really put our heads together and worked as a team,” he said. “It was between fear and a sense of a do-or-die situation.”
“We had to win. We had to pull through and come out on top,” he added.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
Who is the hero pilot?
Hailed as a hero, Indian pilot Smit ​Machchhar was credited by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on X for saving “the lives of 174 people, including Israeli citizens and other nationals.”

Even though he was bleeding heavily, Machchhar managed to unlock the door to the cockpit, Netanyahu told Fox News, allowing crew members and passengers to subdue his colleague and regain control of the plane.
The Indian Embassy in Saudi Arabia said on X that he was admitted to a hospital in Tabuk, where the plane landed, and was “reported to be in stable condition.”

According to his LinkedIn profile, Machchhar, who was also praised on social media by Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, worked with India’s SpiceJet ‌airline for more than 11 years before joining Flydubai. He has logged more than 9,750 flying hours, the profile says.

Machchhar trained as a pilot at Mainland Air in the New Zealand city of Dunedin for 18 months, beginning in 2008, the school’s CEO, Philip Kean, told the country’s 1News outlet. Machchhar “did very well” as a student and later returned to India where he worked as a recruiter for the school, Kean said.
What about the alleged attacker?
Few details have been released about the alleged attacker, including his name and his condition.
Two senior U.S. law enforcement officials briefed on the incident told NBC News that investigators say the pilot who began stabbing the other pilot is from Oman.
Omani authorities have not commented, and the Omani Foreign Ministry and the embassy in Washington did not respond to requests for comment from NBC News.
Netanyahu said the pilot was being investigated in Saudi Arabia, where he was detained after the flight landed.

Both Machchhar and the pilot who initiated the attack were transferred to Abu Dhabi, the capital of the United Arab Emirates, on Thursday, according to a statement from the Saudi Arabian Interior Ministry, citing an unnamed “official source” at the ministry.

“The source confirmed that the pilot and his co-pilot, after their health improved and the medical team cleared them, departed the Kingdom for Abu Dhabi this morning,” the ministry said in the statement.
Was it an attack?

Based on the early results of the investigation, it increasingly looks like this was an act of terrorism, a senior American official and a Saudi Arabian official briefed on the investigation told NBC News.
Saudi Arabia confirmed an altercation between Machchhar and the co-pilot in the Interior Ministry statement posted Thursday.

“The source indicated that initial investigations conducted by the competent authorities in the Kingdom, with the participation of a security team from the sisterly United Arab Emirates, revealed an assault on the pilot by his co-pilot, resulting in both sustaining various injuries,” the ministry said in the statement.

The United Arab Emirates, which owns Flydubai, is also trying to determine “whether the incident was linked to any terrorist activity or ‌purpose, or involved prior planning or direction,” the country’s state news agency reported Thursday.
Without providing any evidence, Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz said Wednesday ⁠that preliminary information indicated that the pilot whom he described as a terrorist aimed to crash the plane.
Netanyahu described it as “a serious security incident.”
Speaking in the Oval Office on Wednesday, President Donald Trump said he had spoken with Netanyahu “at length about this event.”
“It seems as though the co-pilot was perhaps a terrorist or perhaps a whack job, and he stabbed the pilot,” he said.
Was Iran involved?
There are no indications that Iran directed or was involved in the attack, a senior U.S. official briefed on the Israeli investigation told NBC News.

And there have been no official suggestions from Israel that the Islamic Republic was behind the attack. Two Israeli security officials told The Associated Press that Israel had not identified any Iranian involvement so far.
On Thursday, Trump told reporters at the White House that the pilot who initiated the attack could be linked to Iran.
“I would say the answer, based on what I’m hearing, is yes. But we’re working on it right now,” he said.
Asked whether the pilot could have been radicalized or working with Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, Trump replied, “Could have been, yeah.”
Trump also told reporters on Thursday that there would be renewed strikes against Iran if it was behind the attack.
Asked if the U.S. would retaliate against Iran if it was involved in the attack, Trump said, “Oh they’ll be hit very hard, don’t worry.”
“You just ask them,” he added. “They know what happened. They’ll be hit very hard.”
Does it alter anything for American flights?
There are “no credible threats” to U.S. airlines, Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin told a news conference Wednesday.
But he said the U.S. took every incident like this very seriously “and we continue to look at the procedures that we have in place, and continue to make sure the American people are safe.”
What questions remain?
Aside from his nationality, little is known about the pilot who carried out the attack or his motives for doing so.
Pilots undergo rigorous screening, and it is standard for airlines to vet their backgrounds and check their criminal and employment histories.

They also pass through metal detectors and checkpoints at airports, so it is unclear how he sneaked a weapon aboard the plane. Netanyahu said in his interview with Fox News that Machchhar had apparently been stabbed or hit with ⁠an ax.
It also remains unclear whether air marshals were on board the flight at the time of the incident.

Saudi Arabia has warned that it is too early to draw definitive conclusions about who was responsible for the incident, and Israel and the UAE have announced investigations into what exactly happened on Flydubai Flight 1073.

title: What we know about the pilot hailed as a hero for averting crash of Israel-bound plane
summary: He is being hailed around the world as a hero for helping stop a passenger plane bound for Israel from plunging into the ground, despite his own severe injuries.
story: He is being hailed around the world as a hero for helping stop a passenger plane bound for Israel from plunging into the ground, despite his own severe injuries.

Images of Capt. Smit Machchhar covered in blood have gone viral after he fought his fellow pilot, who, according to Israeli officials, stabbed him and attempted to nosedive the plane carrying 174 people from Dubai to Tel Aviv.

While bleeding profusely, Machchhar managed to open the cockpit door, allowing other passengers and the Emirati crew to overpower the other pilot and take control of the aircraft. The flight was diverted to an airport in Saudi Arabia, where it landed safely.

The Mumbai native’s actions have “shown the world the highest form of courage” and “prevented another 9/11-like attack from happening,” Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi said Thursday, after speaking with Machchhar’s family. “The whole world is proud of him,” he added.
Machchhar spoke previously of getting the “aviation bug” at 19 while pursuing a management course to grow his family’s textile business.
He worked for years at a low-cost Indian airline before joining Flydubai and had nearly 10,000 hours of flying experience before Wednesday’s incident.

Machchhar is being treated in a hospital in Tabuk city in northwest Saudi Arabia, with his condition described as “stable” on Wednesday by the Indian Embassy in Riyadh. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu told Fox News he was “very badly wounded.”

Deepak Mittal, India’s ambassador to the United Arab Emirates, said on X he met with Machchhar’s family on Thursday in Dubai and “conveyed full support of the Government of India in ensuring welfare and wellbeing of the Indian Hero.”
Netanyahu called Machchhar “a true hero.”

“Despite being stabbed and seriously injured, he fought back, resisted, opened the cockpit door and enabled passengers and crew to overpower the attacker — preventing a catastrophic midair disaster,” he said.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

Machchhar’s former employer, the Indian budget carrier SpiceJet, said on X that he flew for the airline for 10 years. According to his LinkedIn profile, Machchhar joined the Emirati low-cost carrier Flydubai in 2022 after flying for SpiceJet since 2011.

On Wednesday, the veteran captain was flying a Boeing 737 Max 8, the newer variant of the 737 plane that Machchhar had nearly 10,000 hours of experience flying, according to his profile and a YouTube podcast interview he gave last year.
“My first aircraft was a Boeing, and it’s always been that aircraft all my life,” he said.
Machchhar said he had flown challenging routes, dodged bad weather and handled medical emergencies in the air before.
His mother was “scared” when he first told her of his plan to become a pilot, he said in the 2025 interview, but his supportive father agreed to cover the steep fees for aviation training.

Between 2008 and 2009, Machchhar trained for 18 months at an aviation college in New Zealand. It was the first time he had been outside India, he said, and he had been on only a “couple of flights” as a passenger before learning to fly.
He “stood out” among those training and did well with his studies, Mainland Air chief executive Philip Kean told New Zealand’s 1News, adding: “We’re all very proud of him here.”
In his early days as a qualified pilot, he took whatever flight routes he was assigned.
“When I started flying ... the only thing I wanted to do then was fly,” Machchhar told the podcast. “I didn’t want to sleep, I didn’t want to go anywhere, and they loved me for it.”
“For a pilot to gain that experience and to refine your skills is what a pilot is,” he added.
But his attitude changed when he got married and started a family, he said.
“Now I would say I try when I get out of the cockpit or the aircraft, I don’t want the other guy to know that I’m a pilot. I don’t want to discuss aviation,” he said.
“Now the kids are there,” he said. “They want to play with you.”
In the interview, Machchhar also spoke about the “rigorous training” that pilots and cabin crew undergo, which includes safety and emergency procedures.
“When we are up there and if something happens, who is going to save you? You’ll be lucky enough to have a doctor on board,” he said.
“They can save your life,” he said, referring to the cabin crew.
